因为有限的、或隐晦的性行为本质上是一场参与者力图取胜的斗争，所以它往往指向特定的时刻、结果和最终场景。如同所有有限的游戏一样，它很大程度上依赖于欺骗。性欲通常不会直接表达，而是隐藏在一系列的佯攻、手势、着装风格和炫耀的行为之下。诱惑是精心策划、编写剧本、精心装扮的。人们会寻求特定的回应，并精心设计情节。在高明的诱惑中，会运用拖延战术，并安排特殊的情境和场景。

Seductions are designed to come to an end. Time runs out. The play is finished. All that remains is recollection, the memory of a moment, and perhaps a longing for its repetition. Seductions cannot be repeated. Once one has won or lost in a particular finite game, the game cannot be played over. Moments once reached cannot be reached again. Lovers often sustain vivid reminders of extraordinary moments, but they are reminded at the same time of their impotence in recreating them. The appetite for novelty in lovemaking—new positions, the use of drugs, exotic surroundings, additional partners—is only a search for new moments that can live on only in recollection.

诱惑注定会结束。时间流逝，游戏落幕。留下的只有回忆，对某个瞬间的记忆，或许还有对重温的渴望。诱惑无法重现。一旦在某个有限的游戏中胜负已分，游戏便无法重来。曾经的瞬间，无法再次抵达。恋人们常常对那些非凡的时刻记忆犹新，但同时也意识到自己无力重现。对性爱中新鲜感的追求——新的体位、药物的使用、异国风情、额外的伴侣——不过是对只能存在于回忆中的新瞬间的追寻。

As with all finite play, the goal of veiled sexuality is to bring itself to an end.

就像所有有限的游戏一样，隐秘的性行为的目标是结束自身。

60

By contrast, infinite players have no interest in seduction or in restricting the freedom of another to one’s own boundaries of play. Infinite players recognize choice in all aspects of sexuality. They may see in themselves and in others, for example, the infant’s desire to compete for the mother, but they also see that there is neither physiological nor societal destiny in sexual patterns. Who chooses to compete with another can also choose to play with another.

相比之下，无限玩家对诱惑或将他人的自由限制在自己的游戏边界内毫无兴趣。无限玩家承认性行为各个方面都存在选择。例如，他们或许会在自己和他人身上看到婴儿渴望争夺母亲的心理，但他们也明白，性模式既非生理上的宿命，也非社会上的宿命。选择与他人竞争的人，同样也可以选择与他人玩耍。

Sexuality is not a bounded phenomenon but a horizonal phenomenon for infinite players. One can never say, therefore, that an infinite player is homosexual, or heterosexual, or celibate, or adulterous, or faithful—because each of these definitions has to do with boundaries, with circumscribed areas and styles of play. Infinite players do not play within sexual boundaries, but with sexual boundaries. They are concerned not with power but with vision.

性并非一种界限分明的现象，而是一种面向无限参与者的横向现象。因此，我们永远无法断言一位无限参与者是同性恋、异性恋、独身者、通奸者还是忠贞者——因为这些定义都与界限、与限定的领域和游戏方式相关。无限参与者并非在性界限内游戏，而是与性界限互动。他们关注的不是权力，而是视野。

In their sexual play they suffer others, allow them to be as they are. Suffering others, they open themselves. Open, they learn both about others and about themselves. Learning, they grow. What they learn is not about sexuality, but how to be more concretely and originally themselves, to be the genius of their own actions, to be whole.

在他们的性游戏中，他们包容他人，允许他们保持本真。包容他人，他们敞开自己。敞开自己，他们既了解他人，也了解自己。学习，他们成长。他们所学的并非性本身，而是如何更具体、更真实地做自己，成为自己行为的天才，成为一个完整的人。

Moving therefore from an original center, the sexual engagements of infinite players have no standards, no ideals, no marks of success or failure. Neither orgasm nor conception is a goal in their play, although either may be part of the play.

因此，从最初的中心出发，无数参与者的性行为没有标准，没有理想，也没有成败的标志。高潮和受孕都不是他们游戏的目标，尽管两者都可能是游戏的一部分。

61

There is nothing hidden in infinite sexuality. Sexual desire is exposed as sexual desire and is never therefore serious. Its satisfaction is never an achievement, but an act in a continuing relationship, and therefore joyous. Its lack of satisfaction is never a failure, but only a matter to be taken on into further play.

无限的性欲中没有任何隐藏。性欲本身就是性欲，因此它永远不会显得严肃。性欲的满足并非成就，而是持续关系中的一个环节，因此令人愉悦。性欲的缺失也并非失败，而只是一个需要进一步探索的问题。

Infinite lovers may or may not have a family. Rousseau said the only human institution that is not conventional is the family, which for a brief time is required by nature. Rousseau erred. No family is united by natural or any other kind of necessity. Families can convene only out of choice. The family of infinite lovers has this difference, that it is self-evidently chosen. It is a progressive work of unveiling. Fathering and mothering are roles freely assumed but always with the design of showing them to be theatrical. It is the intention of parents in such families to make it plain to their children that they all play cultural and not societal roles, that they are only roles, and that they are all truly concrete persons behind them. Therefore, children also learn that they have a family only by choosing to have it, by a collective act to be a family with each other.

无限的爱侣们或许有家庭，或许没有。卢梭曾说，唯一非传统的人类制度是家庭，它只是自然在短暂时期内的一种需求。卢梭错了。没有哪个家庭是因自然或其他任何需要而结合的。家庭的形成只能出于选择。无限的爱侣们的家庭与众不同之处在于，它是不言而喻的选择。这是一个逐步揭示的过程。为人父母的角色是自由选择的，但其目的始终在于展现其戏剧性。在这样的家庭中，父母的意图是向孩子们明确表明，他们扮演的是文化角色而非社会角色，这些角色仅仅是角色，而角色背后，他们都是真实存在的个体。因此，孩子们也学会了，他们只有通过选择拥有家庭，通过彼此共同组成家庭的集体行为，才能明白家庭的存在。

62

Infinite sexuality does not focus its attention on certain parts or regions of the body. Infinite lovers have no “private parts.” They do not regard their bodies as having secret zones that can be exposed or made accessible to others for special favors. It is not their bodies but their persons they make accessible to others.

无限的性爱并不关注身体的某些特定部位或区域。无限的爱人没有“私处”。他们不认为自己的身体有可以暴露或为了特殊利益而向他人敞开的秘密区域。他们向他人敞开的不是他们的身体，而是他们的人格。

The paradox of infinite sexuality is that by regarding sexuality as an expression of the person and not the body, it becomes fully embodied play. It becomes a drama of touching.

无限性欲的悖论在于，当性欲被视为人格而非肉体的表达时，它便成为一种完全具象化的游戏，一种触碰的戏剧。

The triumph of finite sexuality is to be liberated from play into the body. The essence of infinite sexuality is to be liberated into play with the body. In finite sexuality I expect to relate to you as a body; in infinite sexuality I expect to relate to you in your body.

有限性爱的胜利在于从玩乐中解放出来，回归身体。无限性爱的本质在于解放出来，回归身体的玩乐。在有限性爱中，我期待与你建立身体层面的关系；在无限性爱中，我期待与你建立身体层面的关系。

Infinite lovers conform to the sexual expectations of others in a way that does not expose something hidden, but unveils something in plain sight: that sexual engagement is a poiesis of free persons. In this exposure they emerge as the persons they are. They meet others with their limitations, and not within their limitations. In doing so they expect to be transformed—and are transformed.

无限的爱侣们顺应他人的性期待，这种顺应并非暴露什么隐秘之物，而是揭示显而易见之事：性爱是自由人的一种诗性表达。在这种坦诚中，他们展现出真实的自我。他们与他人相遇，接纳彼此的局限，而非囿于彼此的局限。如此一来，他们期待被改变——而他们也确实被改变了。

# ↩

# ↩

63

A FINITE GAME OCCURS within a world. The fact that it must be limited temporally, numerically, and spatially means that there is something against which the limits stand. There is an outside to every finite game. Its limits are meaningless unless there is something to be limited, unless there is a larger space, a longer time, a greater number of possible competitors.

有限博弈发生在一个特定的世界中。它在时间、数量和空间上都必须受到限制，这意味着存在某种事物来约束这些限制。任何有限博弈都存在一个外部世界。除非存在需要限制的事物，除非存在更大的空间、更长的时间、更多的潜在竞争者，否则它的限制就毫无意义。

There is nothing about a finite game, in itself, that determines at what time it is to be played, or by whom, or where.

有限游戏本身并没有任何因素决定它在什么时间、由谁玩、在哪里玩。

The rules of a finite game will indicate the temporal, spatial, and numerical nature of the game itself; that, for example, it will last sixty minutes, will be played on a field 100 yards in length, and by two teams of eleven players each. But the rules do not, and cannot, determine the date, the location, and the specific participants. There is nothing in the rules that requires professional teams composed of certain persons, earning salaries of specified amounts, joining at the end of each season in a national championship. The rules for the practice of medicine or for the exercise of the office of the Bishop of Rome do not indicate which persons are to enter these games; which kinds of persons, yes, but never the names of anyone.

有限比赛的规则会规定比赛的时间、空间和数量特征；例如，比赛时长为六十分钟，场地长度为一百码，由两支各十一名球员的队伍进行。但规则不会，也不可能决定比赛的日期、地点和具体参赛者。规则中没有任何条款要求由特定人员组成的职业球队，领取特定数额的薪水，并在每个赛季末参加全国锦标赛。行医或担任罗马主教的规则也不会规定哪些人应该参与这些活动；规则会规定哪些类型的人可以参与，但绝不会规定任何人的姓名。

A world provides an absolute reference without which the time, place, and participants make no sense.

世界提供了一个绝对的参照系，没有它，时间、地点和参与者就毫无意义。

Whatever occurs within a game is relatively intelligible with reference to whatever else has happened inside its boundaries, but it is absolutely intelligible with reference to that world for the sake of which its boundaries exist.

游戏内发生的一切都可以相对于游戏边界内发生的其他事情来理解，但对于游戏边界所代表的那个世界而言，它是完全可以理解的。

It is relatively intelligible to have won an election for the presidency by a few thousand votes after a campaign of about ten months; it is absolutely intelligible to be the sixteenth President of the United States, a society unambiguously marked off from all the rest of the world by its declared boundaries, in the 1,860th year of that world’s history.

经过大约十个月的竞选，以几千票的优势赢得总统选举是相对可以理解的；在世界历史的第1860年，成为美国第十六任总统，而美国作为一个社会，其已宣布的边界与世界其他地区明确区分开来，这完全可以理解。

We cannot have a precise understanding of what it means to be the winner of a contest until we can place the game in the absolute dimensions of a world.

只有当我们能够将比赛置于世界的绝对维度中时，我们才能准确地理解赢得比赛的意义。

64

World exists in the form of audience. A world is not all that is the case, but that which determines all that is the case.

世界以受众的形式存在。世界并非指所有既定事实，而是指决定所有既定事实的因素。

An audience consists of persons observing a contest without participating in it.

观众是指观看比赛而不参与比赛的人。

No one determines who an audience will be. No exercise of power can make a world. A world must be its own spontaneous source. “A world worlds” (Heidegger). Who must be a world cannot be a world.

没有人能够决定谁会成为世界。任何权力的行使都无法创造一个世界。世界必须是其自身自发的源泉。“世界即世界”（海德格尔）。那些自认为必须成为世界的人，反而不可能成为世界。

The number of persons who join an audience is irrelevant. So is the time and space in which an audience occurs. The temporal and spatial boundaries of a finite game must be absolute—in relation to an audience or a world. But when and where a world occurs, and whom it includes, is of no importance. One does not say, “I was in the world, or audience, on November 22, 1963,” but rather, “I was just getting out of the car thinking about what to cook for dinner when I heard that the President had been shot.” An audience does not receive its identity according to the persons within it, but according to the events it observes. Those who remember that day remember precisely what they were doing in the early afternoon of that day, not because it was the 22d of November, but because it was at that moment that they became audience to the events of that day.

加入观众的人数无关紧要。观众出现的时间和空间也同样无关紧要。有限游戏的时空边界必须是绝对的——无论相对于观众还是相对于整个世界而言。但是，一个世界何时何地出现，以及它包含哪些人，都无关紧要。人们不会说“1963年11月22日，我身处那个世界，或者说，我是一个观众”，而是会说“我刚下车，正在想晚饭做什么，就听到总统遇刺的消息”。观众的身份并非取决于其中的人员，而是取决于它所见证的事件。那些记得那天的人之所以能清楚地记得那天下午早些时候他们在做什么，并非因为那天是11月22日，而是因为正是在那一刻，他们成为了那天事件的观众。

If the boundaries of an audience are irrelevant, what is relevant is the unity of the audience. They must be a singular entity, bound in their desire to see who will win the contest before them. Anyone for whom this desire is not primary is not in the audience for that contest, and is not a person in that world.

如果观众的边界无关紧要，那么重要的是观众的团结。他们必须是一个整体，因共同的愿望而紧密相连，那就是见证眼前这场竞赛的胜负。任何不以这种愿望为首要目标的人，都不属于这场竞赛的观众，也不属于那个世界。

The fact that a finite game needs an audience before which it can be played, and the fact that an audience needs to be singularly absorbed in the events before it, show the crucial reciprocity of finite play and the world. Finite players need the world to provide an absolute reference for understanding themselves; simultaneously, the world needs the theater of finite play to remain a world. George Eliot’s villainous character, Grandcourt, “did not care a languid curse for anyone’s admiration; but this state of non-caring, just as much as desire, required its related object—namely, a world of admiring and envying spectators: for if you are fond of looking stonily at smiling persons, the persons must be there and they must smile.”

有限游戏需要观众才能进行，而观众又需要全神贯注于眼前的事件，这一事实揭示了有限游戏与世界之间至关重要的互惠关系。有限游戏的参与者需要世界提供绝对的参照系来理解自身；同时，世界也需要有限游戏的舞台才能继续存在。乔治·艾略特笔下的反派人物格兰考特“丝毫不在意任何人的赞赏；但这种漠不关心的状态，如同欲望一样，需要与之相关的对象——即一个充满赞赏和嫉妒的旁观者的世界：因为如果你喜欢冷眼旁观那些面带微笑的人，那么这些人就必须在那里，而且他们必须面带微笑。”

We are players in search of a world as often as we are world in search of players, and sometimes we are both at once. Some worlds pass quickly into existence, and quickly out of it. Some sustain themselves for longer periods, but no world lasts forever.

我们常常既是寻找世界的玩家，也是寻找玩家的世界，有时两者兼而有之。有些世界转瞬即逝，有些世界则能延续更久，但没有哪个世界能够永恒存在。

65

There is an indefinite number of worlds.

世界的数量是无限的。

66

The reciprocity of game and world has another, deeper effect on the persons involved. Because the seriousness of finite play derives from the players’ need to correct another’s putative assessment of themselves, there is no requirement that the audience be physically present, since players are already their own audience. Just as in finite sexuality where the absence or death of parents has no effect on the child’s determination to prove them wrong, finite players become their own hostile observers in the very act of competing.

游戏与世界的互动对参与者还有更深层次的影响。由于有限游戏的严肃性源于玩家纠正他人对其自身评价的需要，因此无需观众实际在场，因为玩家本身就是自己的观众。正如在有限性行为中，父母的缺席或死亡并不会动摇孩子证明父母错误的决心一样，有限游戏中的玩家在竞争的过程中也成为了自己充满敌意的观察者。

I cannot be a finite player without being divided against myself.

如果我不与自己内心产生冲突，我就无法成为一个有极限的球员。

A similar dynamic is found in the audience. When sufficiently oblivious to their status as audience, the observers of a finite game become so absorbed in its conduct that they lose the sense of distance between themselves and the players. It is they, quite as much as the players, who win or lose. For this reason the audience absorbs in itself the same politics of resentment that moves players to show they are not what they think others think they are. The audience is under the same constraint to disprove this judgment.

类似的动态也存在于观众身上。当观众对自身作为观众的身份感到足够麻木时，他们会完全沉浸于有限博弈的进程中，以至于丧失了与参与者之间的距离感。他们与参与者一样，都参与了博弈的胜负。正因如此，观众自身也吸收了同样的怨恨政治，这种政治驱使参与者去证明自己并非他人眼中的那样。观众同样受到一种约束，那就是要推翻这种评判。

When we ask where an audience will find its own audience, we discover the division inherent in all audiences. Each side of a conflict comes with its own partisan observers. Inasmuch as the conflict is expressed within the bounded playing of a game, the audience is unified—but its unity consists in its opposition to itself.

当我们探究观众群体如何找到自己的受众时，我们会发现所有受众群体都存在固有的分裂。冲突的每一方都有其各自的拥护者。由于冲突是在游戏这一有限的框架内进行的，因此观众群体是统一的——但这种统一性恰恰体现在它与自身的对立之中。

We cannot become a world without being divided against ourselves.

如果我们不进行内部分裂，我们就无法成为一个统一的世界。

67

Occurring before a world, theatrically, a finite game occurs within time. Because it has its boundaries, its beginning and end, within the absolute temporal limits established by a world, time for a finite player runs out; it is used up. It is a diminishing quantity.

在世界面前，戏剧化的有限游戏发生在时间之内。因为它有其边界，有始有终，都局限于世界所设定的绝对时间限制之内，所以对于有限的玩家来说，时间终会耗尽；时间是递减的。

A finite game does not have its own time. It exists in a world’s time. An audience allows players only so much time to win their titles.

有限赛制游戏没有自己的时间，它存在于一个世界的时间框架内。观众只允许选手在有限的时间内赢得冠军。

Early in a game time seems abundant, and there appears a greater freedom to develop future strategies. Late in a game, time is rapidly being consumed. As choices become more limited they become more important. Errors are more disastrous.

游戏初期时间似乎充裕，玩家有更大的自由度来制定未来的策略。但到了游戏后期，时间迅速流逝。随着选择越来越少，每一个选择都变得至关重要，任何失误都可能造成灾难性的后果。

We look on childhood and youth as those “times of life” rich with possibility only because there still seem to remain so many paths open to a successful outcome. Each year that passes, however, increases the competitive value of making strategically correct decisions. The errors of childhood can be more easily amended than those of adulthood.

我们之所以将童年和青年时期视为充满无限可能的“人生阶段”，是因为那时似乎还有许多通往成功的道路。然而，随着岁月的流逝，做出战略性正确决策的竞争价值也日益凸显。童年时期的错误比成年时期的错误更容易弥补。

For the finite player in us freedom is a function of time. We must have time to be free.

对于我们这些有限的个体而言，自由是时间的函数。我们必须拥有时间才能获得自由。

The passage of time is always relative to that which does not pass, to the timeless. Victories occur in time, but the titles won in them are timeless. Titles neither age nor die. The points of reference for all finite history are signal triumphs meant never to be forgotten: establishment of the throne of David, the birth of the Savior, the journey to Medina, the battle of Hastings, the American, French, Russian, Chinese, and Cuban revolutions.

时间的流逝总是相对于那永恒不朽之物而言的。胜利发生在时间之中，但胜利所赢得的头衔却永恒不朽。头衔既不衰老，也不消亡。所有有限历史的参照点都是那些注定永世难忘的标志性胜利：大卫王位的建立、救世主的诞生、麦地那之旅、黑斯廷斯战役、美国革命、法国革命、俄国革命、中国革命和古巴革命。

Time divided into periods is theatrical time. The lapse of time between the opening and closing of an era is a scene between curtains. It is not a time lived, but a time viewed—by both players and audience. The periodization of time presupposes a viewer existing outside the boundaries of play, able to see the beginning and the end simultaneously.

时间被划分成不同的时期，这就是戏剧时间。一个时代从开始到结束的时间间隔，就是幕布之间的场景。这不是一个被体验的时间，而是一个被观看的时间——无论是演员还是观众。时间的划分预设了观众存在于戏剧的边界之外，能够同时看到开始和结束。

The outcome of a finite game is the past waiting to happen. Whoever plays toward a certain outcome desires a particular past. By competing for a future prize, finite players compete for a prized past.

有限博弈的结果，就是等待重现的过去。任何试图达成特定结果的人，都渴望某种特定的过去。通过争夺未来的奖赏，有限博弈的参与者实际上是在争夺一个珍贵的过去。

68

The infinite player in us does not consume time but generates it. Because infinite play is dramatic and has no scripted conclusion, its time is time lived and not time viewed.

我们内心那个无限的玩家并不消耗时间，而是创造时间。因为无限的玩乐充满戏剧性，没有预设的结局，所以它所体验的时间是生活的时间，而非观看的时间。

As an infinite player one is neither young nor old, for one does not live in the time of another. There is therefore no external measure of an infinite player’s temporality. Time does not pass for an infinite player. Each moment of time is a beginning.

作为无限玩家，既非年轻也非年老，因为玩家并不生活在他人的时间之中。因此，无限玩家的时间性没有外部衡量标准。时间对无限玩家而言并不存在。时间的每一刻都是一个新的开始。

Each moment is not the beginning of a period of time. It is the beginning of an event that gives the time within it its specific quality. For an infinite player there is no such thing as an hour of time. There can be an hour of love, or a day of grieving, or a season of learning, or a period of labor.

每个瞬间并非一段时间的开始，而是某个事件的开端，正是这个事件赋予了其中的时间以独特的特质。对于一个无限的玩家而言，并不存在所谓的“一小时”时间。它可以是充满爱意的一小时，也可以是悲伤的一天，可以是学习的季节，也可以是辛勤劳作的时期。

An infinite player does not begin working for the purpose of filling up a period of time with work, but for the purpose of filling work with time. Work is not an infinite player’s way of passing time, but of engendering possibility. Work is not a way of arriving at a desired present and securing it against an unpredictable future, but of moving toward a future which itself has a future.

无限玩家开始工作并非为了用工作填满一段时间，而是为了让时间充满工作本身。工作并非无限玩家消磨时间的方式，而是创造可能性的方式。工作并非抵达理想当下并确保其免受不可预测的未来影响，而是迈向一个本身就拥有未来的未来。

Infinite players cannot say how much they have completed in their work or love or quarreling, but only that much remains incomplete in it. They are not concerned to determine when it is over, but only what comes of it.

无限的玩家无法说清他们在工作、爱情或争吵中完成了多少，他们只知道还有多少未完成。他们并不关心何时结束，只关心最终的结果。

For the finite player in us freedom is a function of time. We must have the time to be free. For the infinite player in us time is a function of freedom. We are free to have time. A finite player puts play into time. An infinite player puts time into play.

对于我们每个人中有限的个体而言，自由是时间的函数。我们必须拥有时间才能获得自由。对于我们每个人中无限的个体而言，时间是自由的函数。我们拥有自由去拥有时间。有限的个体将玩乐融入时间。无限的个体将时间融入玩乐。

69

Just as infinite players can play any number of finite games, so too can they join the audience of any game. They do so, however, for the play that is in observing, quite aware that they are audience. They look, but they see that they are looking.

正如无数玩家可以参与任意数量的有限游戏一样，他们也可以成为任何游戏的观众。然而，他们这样做是为了参与观察本身，并且非常清楚自己是观众。他们观看，但他们也意识到自己正在观看。

Infinite play remains invisible to the finite observer. Such viewers are looking for closure, for the ways in which players can bring matters to a conclusion and finish whatever remains unfinished. They are looking for the way time has exhausted itself, or will soon do so. Finite players stand before infinite play as they stand before art, looking at it, making a poiema of it.

对于有限的观察者而言，无限的游戏始终不可见。这样的观察者寻求的是结局，是玩家如何才能将事情画上句号，完成所有未竟之事。他们寻找的是时间如何耗尽，或者即将耗尽。有限的玩家面对无限的游戏，如同面对艺术一般，凝视着它，从中汲取灵感，创作出诗意的篇章。

If, however, the observers see the poiesis in the work they cease at once being observers. They find themselves in its time, aware that it remains unfinished, aware that their reading of the poetry is itself poetry. Infected then by the genius of the artist they recover their own genius, becoming beginners with nothing but possibility ahead of them.

然而，如果观察者在作品中领悟到诗意，他们便不再是观察者。他们发现自己置身于作品的时代之中，意识到作品尚未完成，意识到他们对诗歌的解读本身就是诗歌。于是，他们被艺术家的天才所感染，重拾自身的天赋，成为拥有无限可能的初学者。

If the goal of finite play is to win titles for their timelessness, and thus eternal life for oneself, the essence of infinite play is the paradoxical engagement with temporality that Meister Eckhart called “eternal birth.”

如果有限游戏的目的是为了赢得永恒的头衔，从而为自己赢得永生，那么无限游戏的本质就是与时间性的悖论式互动，正如埃克哈特大师所说的“永恒的诞生”。

# ↩

# ↩

70

N ATURE IS the realm of the unspeakable. It has no voice of its own, and nothing to say. We experience the unspeakability of nature as its utter indifference to human culture.

自然是不可言说的领域。它没有自己的声音，也无话可说。我们体验到自然的不可言说，便是它对人类文化的全然漠视。

The Master Player in us tolerates this indifference scarcely at all. Indeed, we respond to it as a challenge, an invitation to confrontation and struggle. If nature will offer us no home, offer us nothing at all, we will then clear and arrange a space for ourselves. We take nature on as an opponent to be subdued for the sake of civilization. We count among the highest achievements of modern society the development of a technology that allows us to master nature’s vagaries.

我们内心深处的“大师”几乎无法容忍这种冷漠。事实上，我们将其视为挑战，视为对抗和斗争的邀请。如果大自然不给我们提供家园，什么也不给我们，那么我们就清理并为自己开辟一片空间。我们把大自然视为对手，为了文明的需要而征服它。我们认为，现代社会最伟大的成就之一，就是发展出能够让我们驾驭大自然变幻莫测的科技。

The effort has largely taken the form of theatricalizing our relation to nature. Like any Master Player we have been patiently attentive to the slightest clues in our opponent’s behavior—as a way of preparing ourselves against surprise. Like hunters stalking their prey, we have learned to mimic the movements of nature, waiting for the chance to take hold of them before they get away from us. “Nature, to be commanded, must be obeyed” (Bacon). It is as though, by learning its secret script, we have learned to direct its play as well. There is little left to surprise us.

这种努力很大程度上表现为将我们与自然的关系戏剧化。如同任何一位技艺精湛的演员，我们耐心地留意着对手行为中最细微的线索——以此来防范突袭。如同猎人潜伏猎物，我们学会了模仿自然的行动，等待着在它们逃脱之前将其掌控。“要驾驭自然，就必须服从它”（培根）。仿佛通过学习自然的秘密剧本，我们也学会了执导它的戏剧。如今，已没有什么能让我们感到意外了。

The assumption guiding our struggle against nature is that deep within itself nature contains a structure, an order, that is ultimately intelligible to the human understanding. Since this inherent structure determines the way things change, and is not itself subject to change, we speak of nature being lawful, of repeating itself according to quite predictable patterns.

我们与自然抗争的根本假设是，自然本身蕴含着一种结构和秩序，最终是人类能够理解的。由于这种内在结构决定了事物变化的方式，而它本身却不会改变，所以我们说自然是有规律的，会按照相当可预测的模式重复自身。

What we have done by showing that certain events repeat themselves according to known laws is to explain them. Explanation is the mode of discourse in which we show why matters must be as they are. All laws made use of in explanation look backward in time from the conclusion or the completion of a sequence. It is implicit in all explanatory discourse that just as there is a discoverable necessity in the outcome of past events, there is a discoverable necessity in future events. What can be explained can also be predicted, if one knows the initial events and the laws covering their succession. A prediction is but an explanation in advance.

我们通过证明某些事件会按照已知的规律重复发生，从而对其进行解释。解释是一种论述方式，它阐明事物为何必然如此。所有用于解释的规律都从某个序列的结束或完成回溯过去。所有解释性论述都隐含着这样一个观点：正如过去事件的结果存在可发现的必然性一样，未来事件也存在可发现的必然性。如果知道初始事件及其发展规律，那么可以解释的事物也可以预测。预测本质上就是一种预先的解释。

Because of its thorough lawfulness nature has no genius of its own. On the contrary, it is sometimes thought that the grandest discovery of the human genius is the perfect compatibility between the structure of the natural order and the structure of the mind, thereby making a complete understanding of nature possible. “One may say ‘the eternal mystery of the world is its comprehensibility’” (Einstein).

由于自然界的彻底规律性，它本身并无天才可言。相反，人们有时认为，人类最伟大的天才发现，在于自然秩序的结构与思维结构的完美契合，从而使我们对自然的全面理解成为可能。“我们可以说，‘世界永恒的奥秘在于它的可理解性’”（爱因斯坦）。

This is as much as to say that nature does have a voice, and its voice is no different from our own. We can then presume to speak for the unspeakable.

这相当于说，大自然确实有自己的声音，而且它的声音与我们自己的声音并无二致。如此一来，我们便可以妄自为那些不可言说之事代言。

This achievement is often raised as a sign of the great superiority of modern civilization over the many faded and lost civilizations of the ancients. While our great skill lies in finding patterns of repetition under the apparent play of accident and chance, less successful civilizations dealt with the threats of natural accident by appealing to supernatural powers for protection. But the voices of the gods proved to be ignorant and false; they have been silenced by the truth.

这一成就常被视为现代文明远胜于众多已消逝的古代文明的标志。我们真正的优势在于善于在看似偶然和巧合的表象下发现重复出现的模式，而那些不太成功的文明则诉诸超自然力量来应对自然灾害的威胁。然而，事实证明，神明的声音既无知又虚假；它们已被真理所压制。

71

There is an irony in our silencing of the gods. By presuming to speak for the unspeakable, by hearing our own voice as the voice of nature, we have had to step outside the circle of nature. It is one thing for physics and chemistry to be speaking about nature; it is quite another for physics and chemistry to be the speaking of nature. No chemist would want to say that chemistry is itself chemical, for our speaking cannot be both chemical and about chemistry. If speaking about a process is itself part of the process, there is something that must remain permanently hidden from the speaker. To be intelligible at all, we must claim that we can step aside from the process and comment on it “objectively” and “dispassionately,” without anything obstructing our view of these matters. Here lies the irony: By way of this perfectly reasonable claim the gods have stolen back into our struggle with nature. By depriving the gods of their own voices, the gods have taken ours. It is we who speak as supernatural intelligences and powers, masters of the forces of nature.

我们让神祇噤声，这其中蕴含着讽刺。我们妄图为不可言说之物代言，将自身的声音视为自然之声，却不得不置身于自然之外。物理和化学谈论自然是一回事，而物理和化学本身就是自然的代言人，则是另一回事。没有哪个化学家会愿意说化学本身就是化学，因为我们的言辞不可能既是化学的，又是关于化学的。如果谈论某个过程本身就是该过程的一部分，那么就必然有某些东西对说话者而言是永远隐藏的。为了使我们的言辞能够被理解，我们必须声称自己可以置身于过程之外，以“客观”和“冷静”的态度对其进行评述，不受任何事物的干扰。讽刺之处在于：正是凭借这种看似合理的主张，神祇重新介入了我们与自然的斗争。通过剥夺神祇自身的话语权，神祇夺走了我们的声音。我们以超自然智慧和力量的化身，自然力量的主宰者的身份发言。

This irony passes unnoticed only so long as we continue to veil ourselves against what we can otherwise plainly see: nature allows no master over itself. Bacon’s principle works both ways. If we must obey to command, then our commanding is only obeying and not commanding at all. There is no such thing as an unnatural act. Nothing can be done to or against nature, much less outside it. Therefore, the ignorance we thought we could avoid by an unclouded observation of nature has swept us back into itself. What we thought we read in nature we discover we have read into nature. “We have to remember that what we observe is not nature in itself but nature exposed to our method of questioning” (Heisenberg).

这种讽刺之所以不为人知，仅仅是因为我们继续蒙蔽自己，对显而易见的事实视而不见：自然不允许任何人凌驾于自身之上。培根的原则是双向的。如果我们必须服从命令，那么我们的命令就只是服从，而非真正的命令。根本不存在所谓的反自然行为。任何事都不能针对自然，更不能违背自然。因此，我们原本以为可以通过对自然的清晰观察来避免无知，结果却反而将我们卷入了自然本身。我们以为从自然中读到的东西，最终却发现我们只是把自然本身解读成了自然的一部分。“我们必须记住，我们所观察到的并非自然本身，而是自然在我们提问方式的影响下呈现出来的样子”（海森堡）。

72

We are speaking now of no ordinary ignorance. It is not what we could have known but do not; it is unintelligibility itself: that which no mind can ever comprehend.

我们现在所说的绝非普通的无知。它并非我们本可以知道却不知道的事情；而是不可理解本身：任何头脑都永远无法理解的事物。

Unveiled, aware of the insuperable limitation placed against all our looking, we come back to nature’s perfect silence. Now we can see that it is a silence so complete there is no way of knowing what it is silent about—if anything. What we learn from this silence is the unlikeness between nature and whatever we could think or say about it. But this silence has an irony of its own: Far from stupefying us, it provides an indispensable condition to the mind’s own originality. By confronting us with radical unlikeness, nature becomes the source of metaphor.

揭开面纱，意识到我们所有观察都受到不可逾越的限制，我们回归到自然完美的寂静之中。如今我们明白，这是一种如此彻底的寂静，以至于我们根本无法知晓它究竟在沉默什么——如果它真的在沉默的话。我们从这种寂静中领悟到的是，自然与我们所能思考或描述的一切截然不同。然而，这种寂静本身也蕴含着一种讽刺：它非但没有使我们麻木，反而为心灵的独创性提供了不可或缺的条件。通过让我们直面这种根本性的差异，自然成为了隐喻的源泉。

Metaphor is the joining of like to unlike such that one can never become the other. Metaphor requires an irreducibility, an imperturbable indifference of its terms for one another. The falcon can be the “kingdom of daylight’s dauphin” only if the daylight could have no dauphin, could indeed have nothing to do with dauphins.

隐喻是将相似事物与不相似事物并置，使二者之间永不相容。隐喻要求其具有不可还原性，要求其所指称的事物彼此之间保持绝对的漠然。只有当白昼本身没有王太子，与王太子毫无关联时，猎鹰才能被称为“白昼王国的太子”。

At its root all language has the character of metaphor, because no matter what it intends to be about it remains language, and remains absolutely unlike whatever it is about. This means that we can never have the falcon, only the word “falcon.” To say that we have the falcon, and not the “falcon,” is to presume again that we know precisely what it is we have, that we can see it in its entirety, and that we can speak as nature itself.

语言的本质在于其隐喻性，因为无论它意在描述什么，它始终是语言，并且与它所描述的对象截然不同。这意味着我们永远无法拥有猎鹰本身，而只能拥有“猎鹰”这个词。说我们拥有猎鹰而非“猎鹰”这个词，就等于再次假定我们确切地知道我们拥有的是什么，我们能够看到它的全貌，并且我们能够像自然本身那样说话。

The unspeakability of nature is the very possibility of language.

自然界的不可言说性恰恰是语言存在的可能性。

Our attempt to take control of nature, to be Master Player in our opposition to it, is an attempt to rid ourselves of language. It is the refusal to accept nature as “nature.” It is to deafen ourselves to metaphor, and to make nature into something so familiar it is essentially an extension of our willing and speaking. What the hunter kills is not the deer, but the metaphor of the deer—the “deer.” Killing the deer is not an act against nature; it is an act against language. To kill is to impose a silence that remains a silence. It is the reduction of an unpredictable vitality to a predictable mass, the transformation of the remote into the familiar. It is to rid oneself of the need to attend to its otherness.

我们试图掌控自然，试图在与自然对抗中占据主导地位，这实际上是一种摆脱语言的尝试。它拒绝接受自然本身就是“自然”。它使我们对隐喻充耳不闻，并将自然变成某种如此熟悉的事物，以至于它本质上是我们意志和言语的延伸。猎人猎杀的并非鹿本身，而是鹿的隐喻——“鹿”本身。猎杀鹿并非对抗自然，而是对抗语言。杀戮是强加一种始终保持沉默的沉默。它将变幻莫测的生命力简化为可预测的整体，将遥远的事物转化为熟悉的事物。它使我们摆脱了关注其“他者性”的必要。

The physicists who look at their objects within their limitations teach physics; those who see the limitations they place around their objects teach “physics.” For them physics is a poiesis.

那些在研究对象自身局限性范围内进行考察的物理学家，教授的是物理学；而那些看到自己给研究对象设定的局限性的物理学家，教授的却是“物理学”。对他们而言，物理学是一种诗性。

73

If nature is the realm of the unspeakable, history is the realm of the speakable. Indeed, no speaking is possible that is not itself historical. Students of history, like students of nature, often believe they can find unbiased, direct views of events. They look in on the lives of others, noting the multitude of ways those lives have been limited by the age in which they were lived. But no one can look in on an age, even if it is one’s own age, without looking out of an age as well. There is no refuge outside history for such viewers, any more than there is a vantage outside nature.

如果说自然是不可言说的领域，那么历史就是可言说的领域。事实上，任何言说都离不开历史本身。历史研究者，如同自然研究者一样，常常认为自己能够找到客观、直接的事件视角。他们窥视他人的生活，注意到这些生活如何受到所处时代的种种限制。然而，即便审视的是自己的时代，任何人也无法脱离时代而审视自身。对于这样的观察者而言，历史之外无处可逃，正如自然之外无处可观一样。

Since history is the drama of genius, its relentless surprise tempts us into designing boundaries for it, searching through it for patterns of repetition. Historians sometimes speak of trends, of cycles, of currents, of forces, as though they were describing natural events. In doing so they must dehistoricize themselves, taking a perspective from the timeless, believing that each observed history is always of others and never of themselves, that each observation is of history but not itself historical.

历史是天才的戏剧，它无休止的惊喜诱使我们去为其设定界限，从中寻找重复的模式。历史学家有时谈论趋势、周期、潮流和力量，仿佛在描述自然现象。这样做，他们必须将自身去历史化，从永恒的视角出发，相信每一次被观察到的历史都与他人有关，而非与自身有关；每一次观察都与历史有关，但自身却并非历史。

Genuine historians therefore reverse the assumption of the observers of nature that the observation itself cannot be an act of nature. Historians who understand themselves to be historical abandon explanation altogether. The mode of discourse appropriate to such self-aware history is narrative.

因此，真正的历史学家颠覆了自然观察者们的假设，即观察本身不可能是自然行为。那些自视为历史学家的历史学家彻底放弃了解释。适合这种具有自觉意识的历史的论述方式是叙事。

Like explanation, narrative is concerned with a sequence of events and brings its tale to a conclusion. However, there is no general law that makes this outcome necessary. In a genuine story there is no law that makes any act necessary. Explanations place all apparent possibilities into the context of the necessary; stories set all necessities into the context of the possible.

与解释一样，叙事也关注一系列事件，并最终将故事引向结局。然而，并没有什么普遍规律使得这个结局必然发生。在一个真正的故事中，没有任何规律使得任何行为是必然的。解释将所有看似可能的事情置于必然性的语境中；而故事则将所有必然性置于可能性的语境中。

Explanation can tolerate a degree of chance, but it cannot comprehend freedom at all. We explain nothing when we say that persons do whatever they do because they choose to do it. On the other hand, causation cannot find a place in narrative. We have not told a story when we show that persons do whatever they do because they were caused to do it—by their genes, their social circumstances, or the influence of the gods.

解释可以容忍一定程度的偶然性，但它完全无法理解自由。当我们说人们做任何事都是因为他们自己选择这样做时，我们实际上什么也没解释。另一方面，因果关系在叙事中也找不到立足之地。当我们表明人们做任何事是因为他们受到某种因素的影响——基因、社会环境或神灵的影响——时，我们并没有讲述一个完整的故事。

Explanations settle issues, showing that matters must end as they have. Narratives raise issues, showing that matters do not end as they must but as they do. Explanation sets the need for further inquiry aside; narrative invites us to rethink what we thought we knew.

解释旨在解决问题，表明事情必然如此结束。叙事则提出问题，表明事情并非必然如此结束，而是以现在的方式结束。解释搁置了进一步探究的必要性；叙事则邀请我们重新思考我们自以为知道的事情。

If the silence of nature is the possibility of language, language is the possibility of history.

如果说大自然的沉默是语言的可能性，那么语言就是历史的可能性。

74

Successful explanations do not draw attention to themselves as modes of speaking, because what is explained is not itself subject to history. If I explain to you why cold water sinks to the bottom of the pond and ice rises to the surface, I certainly do not intend my explanation to be true now and not later. The explanation is true anywhere and any time.

成功的解释不会刻意强调其自身的表达方式，因为被解释的内容本身不受历史的限制。如果我向你解释为什么冷水会沉到池塘底部，冰会浮到水面，我当然不是指我的解释现在正确而将来不正确。这个解释在任何时间、任何地点都成立。

That I choose to explain this to you in this time and place, however, is historical; it is an event—the narrative of our relation with each other. There must therefore be a reason for the speaking of this verity. Explanations are not offered gratuitiously, just because, say, ice happens to float. I can explain nothing to you unless I first draw your attention to patent inadequacies in your knowledge: discontinuities in the relations between objects, or the presence of anomalies you cannot account for by any of the laws known to you. You will remain deaf to my explanations until you suspect yourself of falsehood.

然而，我选择在此时此地向你解释这一切，具有历史意义；它是一件事件——是我们彼此关系的叙事。因此，我之所以要讲述这个真理，必然有其原因。解释并非无缘无故地提供，比如说，仅仅因为冰碰巧会漂浮。除非我首先让你注意到你知识中显而易见的不足：事物之间关系的断裂，或者你无法用任何已知定律解释的异常现象，否则我无法向你解释任何事情。除非你开始怀疑自己的错误，否则你将对我的解释充耳不闻。

Many of these suspicions are, of course, minor, requiring merely small adjustments in one’s views, incurring no doubt whatsoever concerning those views. Major challenges, however, are too serious to be met with argument, or with sharpened explanation. They call either for outright and wholesale rejection, or for conversion. One does not cross over from Manichaeism to Christianity, or from Lamarckianism to Darwinism, by a mere adjustment of views. True conversions consist in the choice of a new audience, that is, of a new world. All that was once familiar is now seen in startlingly new ways.

当然，这些疑虑大多微不足道，只需对自身观点稍作调整，便不会对其产生任何怀疑。然而，重大的挑战却过于严峻，无法用辩论或更深入的解释来应对。它们要么需要彻底的全盘否定，要么需要彻底的皈依。一个人不可能仅仅通过调整观点就从摩尼教转向基督教，或者从拉马克主义转向达尔文主义。真正的皈依在于选择一个新的受众，也就是一个新的世界。所有曾经熟悉的事物，如今都以令人震惊的全新视角呈现。

As theatrical as conversions are, they remain oblivious to the degree to which choice is involved in the passage from one world to another. Radical conversions, especially, veil themselves against their own arbitrariness. Augustine, the most famous convert of antiquity, was puzzled that he could have held so firmly to so many different falsehoods; he was not astounded that there are so many different truths. His conversion was not from explanation to narrative, but from one explanation to another. When he crossed the line from paganism to Christianity, he arrived in the territory of a truth beyond further challenge.

尽管皈依基督教的过程充满戏剧性，但它们却忽略了从一个世界过渡到另一个世界的过程中，选择所扮演的重要角色。尤其是激进的皈依，往往会掩盖自身的任意性。古代最著名的皈依者奥古斯丁曾困惑于自己为何会如此坚定地坚持如此多的谬论；但他并不惊讶于世间存在如此多的真理。他的皈依并非从解释转向叙事，而是从一种解释转向另一种解释。当他从异教信仰跨入基督教时，他便进入了一个不容置疑的真理领域。

Explanations succeed only by convincing resistant hearers of their error. If you will not hear my explanations until you are suspicious of your own truths, you will not accept my explanations until you are convinced of your error. Explanation is an antagonistic encounter that succeeds by defeating an opponent. It possesses the same dynamic of resentment found in other finite play. I will press my explanations on you because I need to show that I do not live in the error that I think others think I do.

只有当那些固执己见的听众意识到自己的错误时，解释才能成功。如果你非要等到自己开始怀疑自己的真理才肯听我的解释，那么在你确信自己错了之前，你也不会接受我的解释。解释是一种对抗性的交锋，它的成功在于战胜对手。它与其他有限博弈一样，都蕴含着怨恨的动力。我会坚持向你解释，因为我需要证明，我并没有像别人认为的那样，深陷于错误的泥潭之中。

Whoever wins this struggle is privileged with the claim to true knowledge. Knowledge has been arrived at, it is the outcome of this engagement. Its winners have the uncontested power to make certain statements of fact. They are to be listened to. In those areas appropriate to the contests now concluded, winners possess a knowledge that no longer can be challenged.

这场斗争的胜者将享有掌握真知的特权。知识已经产生，它是这场博弈的成果。胜者拥有无可争议的权力来陈述某些事实。他们的声音必须被倾听。在那些与已结束的斗争相关的领域，胜者所拥有的知识已不容置疑。

Knowledge, therefore, is like property. It must be published, declared, or in some other way so displayed that others cannot but take account of it. It must stand in their way. It must be emblematic, pointing backward at its possessor’s competitive skill.

因此，知识如同财产。它必须被公开、宣告或以其他方式展示，使他人不得不重视。它必须成为他人的阻碍。它必须具有象征意义，向世人展现其拥有者的竞争优势。

So close are knowledge and property that they are often thought to be continuous. Those who are entitled to knowledge feel they should be granted property as well, and those who are entitled to property believe a certain knowledge goes with it. Scholars demand higher salaries for their publishable successes; industrialists sit on university boards.

知识与财产如此紧密相连，以至于人们常常认为二者密不可分。那些有权拥有知识的人认为自己也应该拥有财产，而那些有权拥有财产的人则认为某些知识是财产的必然组成部分。学者们要求因其发表的学术成果而获得更高的薪酬；实业家们则占据大学董事会席位。

75

If explanation, to be successful, must be oblivious to the silence of nature, it must also in its success impose silence on its listeners. Imposed silence is the first consequence of the Master Player’s triumph.

如果解释要想成功，就必须无视自然的寂静，那么它的成功也必然会使听众噤声。这种噤声正是大师级演绎者胜利的首要结果。

What one wins in a title is the privilege of magisterial speech. The privilege of magisterial speech is the highest honor attaching to any title. We expect the first act of a winner to be a speech. The first act of the loser may also be a speech, but it will be a speech to concede victory, to declare there will be no further challenge to the winner. It is a speech that promises to silence the loser’s voice.

头衔赋予人的是发表权威演说的特权。这种特权是任何头衔所能附带的最高荣誉。我们期待胜利者的第一件事就是发表演说。失败者的第一件事也可能是发表演说，但这会是承认胜利、宣布不再对胜利者提出任何挑战的演说。这是一篇旨在让失败者噤声的演说。

The silence to which the losers pledge themselves is the silence of obedience. Losers have nothing to say; nor have they an audience who would listen. The vanquished are effectively of one will with the victors, and of one mind; they are completely incapable of opposition, and therefore without any otherness whatsoever.

失败者所宣誓的沉默，乃是服从的沉默。失败者无话可说，也无人倾听。战败者与胜利者实际上意志一致，心意相通；他们完全丧失了反抗的能力，因此也丧失了任何异己性。

The victorious do not speak with the defeated; they speak for the defeated. Husbands speak for wives in the finite family, and parents for their children. Kings speak for the realm, governors for the state, popes for the church. Indeed, the titled, as titled, cannot speak with anyone.

胜利者不与失败者交谈，而是为失败者代言。在有限的家庭中，丈夫为妻子代言，父母为子女代言。君王为王国代言，统治者为国家代言，教皇为教会代言。的确，拥有爵位者，作为爵位本身，不能与任何人交谈。

It is chiefly in magisterial speech that the power of winners resides. To be powerful is to have one’s words obeyed. It is only by magisterial speech that the emblematic property of winners can be safeguarded. Those entitled to their possessions have the privilege of calling the police, calling up an army, to force the recognition of their emblems.

胜利者的权力主要体现在权威的言辞中。真正的权力在于言辞的权威性。也只有通过权威的言辞，胜利者的象征性财产才能得到保障。那些有权拥有这些财产的人，可以动用一切手段，例如报警、征召军队，来强制他人承认他们的象征物。

The power of gods is known principally through their utterances. The sicut dixit dominus (thus says the lord) is always a signal for ritual silence. The speech of a god can be so perfectly expressive of that god’s power that the god and its speech become identical: “In the beginning was the word. The word was with God, and the word was God.”

神的力量主要通过他们的言语来展现。“sicut dixit dominus”（主如此说）总是仪式静默的信号。神的言语可以如此完美地表达其力量，以至于神与神的言语融为一体：“太初有道，道与神同在，道就是神。”

One is speechless before a god, or silent before a winner, because it no longer matters to others what one has to say. To lose a contest is to become obedient; to become obedient is to lose one’s listeners. The silence of obedience is an unheard silence. It is the silence of death. For this reason the demand for obedience is inherently evil.

在神面前，人会哑口无言；在胜利者面前，人会沉默不语，因为别人已不再在意自己说了什么。输掉比赛意味着屈服；屈服意味着失去听众。屈服的沉默是无人听见的沉默，是死亡的沉默。因此，要求服从本身就是邪恶的。

The silence of nature is the possibility of language. By subduing nature the gods give it their own voice, but in making nature an opponent they make all their listeners opponents. By refusing the silence of nature they demand the silence of obedience. The unspeakability of nature is therefore transformed into the unspeakability of language itself.

自然的沉默蕴含着语言的可能性。神明征服自然，赋予其自身的声音，但同时也使自然成为他们的对立面，从而使所有聆听者都成为他们的对立面。他们拒绝接受自然的沉默，从而要求人们保持服从的沉默。因此，自然的不可言说性最终转化为语言本身的不可言说性。

76

Infinite speech is that mode of discourse that consistently reminds us of the unspeakability of nature. It bears no claim to truth, originating from nothing but the genius of the speaker. Infinite speech is therefore not about anything; it is always to someone. It is not command, but address. It belongs entirely to the speakable.

无限言语是一种始终提醒我们自然不可言说的论述方式。它不声称自己拥有真理，其源头仅仅在于说话者的天赋。因此，无限言语并非关于任何事物，而是始终指向某个人。它不是命令，而是呼唤。它完全属于可言说的范畴。

That language is not about anything gives it its status as metaphor. Metaphor does not point at something there. Never shall we find the kingdom of daylight’s dauphin in one place or another. It is not the role of metaphor to draw our sight to what is there, but to draw our vision toward what is not there and, indeed, cannot be anywhere. Metaphor is horizonal, reminding us that it is one’s vision that is limited, and not what one is viewing.

语言本身并不指向任何具体事物，这赋予了它隐喻的地位。隐喻并不指向任何现成的事物。我们永远无法在某个地方找到白昼之王的王国。隐喻的作用并非引导我们关注现成之物，而是引导我们关注不存在之物，事实上，它也不可能存在于任何地方。隐喻是横向的，它提醒我们，受限的是我们的视野，而非我们所看到的事物。

The meaning of a finite speaker’s discourse lies in what precedes its utterance, what is already the case and therefore is the case whether or not it is spoken.

有限说话者的话语的意义在于其话语之前的状态，在于它已经存在的状态，因此无论是否说出口，它都是如此。

The meaning of an infinite speaker’s discourse lies in what comes of its utterance—that is, whatever is the case because it is spoken.

无限说话者的话语的意义在于其话语所产生的结果——也就是说，因为说了这句话而发生的一切。

Finite language exists complete before it is spoken. There is first a language— then we learn to speak it. Infinite language exists only as it is spoken. There is first a language— when we learn to speak it. It is in this sense that infinite discourse always arises from a perfect silence.

有限语言在被说出之前就已经完整存在。先有语言，然后我们才学会说。无限语言只有在被说出时才存在。先有语言，然后我们才学会说。正是在这个意义上，无限的话语总是从完美的寂静中产生。

Finite speakers come to speech with their voices already trained and rehearsed. They must know what they are doing with the language before they can speak it. Infinite speakers must wait to see what is done with their language by the listeners before they can know what they have said. Infinite speech does not expect the hearer to see what is already known to the speaker, but to share a vision the speaker could not have had without the response of the listener.

有限语言的使用者在开口说话之前，就已经训练并排练过他们的声音。他们必须先了解自己在用语言做什么，才能开口说话。无限语言的使用者则必须等待听众如何运用他们的语言，才能知道自己说了什么。无限语言并不期望听众理解使用者早已知晓的内容，而是希望听众分享使用者无法获得的洞见，而这需要听众的回应。

Speaker and listener understand each other not because they have the same knowledge about something, and not because they have established a likeness of mind, but because they know “how to go on” with each other (Wittgenstein).

说话者和听者能够互相理解，不是因为他们对某事有相同的知识，也不是因为他们建立了相似的思想，而是因为他们知道如何与对方“继续”下去（维特根斯坦）。

77

Because it is address, attending always on the response of the addressed, infinite speech has the form of listening. Infinite speech does not end in the obedient silence of the hearer, but continues by way of the attentive silence of the speaker. It is not a silence into which speech has died, but a silence from which speech is born.

因为无限言语是一种呼唤，它始终关注被呼唤者的回应，所以它具有聆听的形式。无限言语并非止于听者顺从的沉默，而是通过说话者专注的沉默而延续。它不是言语消亡的沉默，而是言语诞生的沉默。

Infinite speakers do not give voice to another, but receive it from another. Infinite speakers do not therefore appeal to a world as audience, do not speak before a world, but present themselves as an audience by way of talking with others. Finite speech informs another about the world—for the sake of being heard. Infinite speech forms a world about the other—for the sake of listening.

无限的言语者并非赋予他人声音，而是从他人那里接收声音。因此，无限的言语者并非面向世界发声，也并非在世界面前讲话，而是通过与他人的对话，将自身呈现为听众。有限的言语是为了被倾听而向他人传递关于世界的信息。无限的言语则是为了聆听而构建一个关于他人的世界。

It is for this reason that the gods, insofar as they speak as the lords of this world, magisterially, speak before this world and are therefore unable to change it. Such gods cannot create a world but can only be creations of a world—can only be idols. A god cannot create a world and be magisterial within it. “The religions which represent divinity as commanding whenever it has the power to do so seem false. Even though they are monotheistic they are idolatrous” (Weil).

正因如此，诸神以世界主宰的身份，以权威的姿态发声，他们只是在这个世界面前发声，因此无法改变世界。这样的神无法创造世界，只能是世界的产物——只能是偶像。神无法创造世界，又无法在世界内部拥有至高无上的权威。“那些将神性描绘成只要有能力就发号施令的宗教，似乎是虚假的。即使它们是一神论的，它们也是偶像崇拜”（韦伊）。

A god can create a world only by listening.

神只有聆听才能创造世界。

Were the gods to address us it would not be to bring us to silence through their speech, but to bring us to speech through their silence.

如果神明要对我们说话，那不是为了通过言语使我们沉默，而是为了通过沉默使我们开口说话。

The contradiction of finite speech is that it must end by being heard. The paradox of infinite speech is that it continues only because it is a way of listening. Finite speech ends with a silence of closure. Infinite speech begins with a disclosure of silence.

有限言语的矛盾之处在于，它必须以被聆听而告终。无限言语的悖论在于，它之所以持续，仅仅是因为它是一种聆听的方式。有限言语以闭幕的沉默告终。无限言语始于对沉默的揭示。

78

Storytellers do not convert their listeners; they do not move them into the territory of a superior truth. Ignoring the issue of truth and falsehood altogether, they offer only vision. Storytelling is therefore not combative; it does not succeed or fail. A story cannot be obeyed. Instead of placing one body of knowledge against another, storytellers invite us to return from knowledge to thinking, from a bounded way of looking to an horizonal way of seeing.

讲故事的人不会改变听众的观念；他们不会引导听众进入更高层次的真理领域。他们完全忽略真假的问题，仅仅提供一种视角。因此，讲故事不具对抗性；它既无成败之分，也无所谓服从。故事本身并不要求我们盲从。讲故事的人并不将一种知识体系与另一种知识体系对立起来，而是邀请我们从知识回归思考，从局限的视角回归更广阔的视野。

Infinite speakers are Plato’s poietai taking their place in the historical. Storytellers enter the historical not when their speaking is full of anecdotes about actual persons, or when they appear as characters in their own tales, but when in their speaking we begin to see the narrative character of our lives. The stories they tell touch us. What we thought was an accidental sequence of experiences suddenly takes the dramatic shape of unresolved narrative.

无限的讲述者如同柏拉图笔下的“波耶泰”（poietai），在历史中占据着一席之地。讲述者进入历史，并非因为他们的讲述充满了关于真实人物的轶事，也并非因为他们以自身故事中的角色出现，而是因为他们的讲述让我们开始看到自身生活的叙事特征。他们讲述的故事触动了我们。我们原本以为只是一系列偶然的经历，突然间呈现出未解之谜般的戏剧性叙事形态。

There is no narrative without structure, or plot. In a great story this structure seems like fate, like an inescapable judgment descending on its still unaware heroes, a great metaphysical causality that crowds out all room for choice. Fate arises not as a limitation on our freedom, but as a manifestation of our freedom, testimony that choice is consequent. The exercise of your freedom cannot prevent the exercise of my own freedom, but it can determine the context in which I am to act freely. You cannot make choices for me, but you can largely determine what my choices will be about. Great stories explore the drama of this deeper touching of one free person by another. They are therefore genuinely sexual dramas astounding us once more with the magic of origins.

没有结构或情节，就没有叙事。在伟大的故事中，这种结构如同命运，如同无可逃避的审判降临在懵懂无知的英雄身上，如同巨大的形而上学因果律，挤占了所有选择的余地。命运并非对我们自由的限制，而是我们自由的体现，证明选择必然产生后果。你行使自由并不能阻止我行使自由，但它可以决定我自由行动的语境。你不能替我做选择，但你很大程度上可以决定我的选择是什么。伟大的故事探索了自由之人与自由之人之间这种更深层次的触动所引发的戏剧性冲突。因此，它们是真正意义上的性爱戏剧，再次以起源的魔力震撼着我们。

The myth of Oedipus is one of many great sexual narratives in the cultural treasury of the West that plays on the dramatic relation of fate and origin. Once Oedipus had impulsively killed Laius, not knowing he was his own father, he was carried ahead by ambition and lust into marriage with the dead man’s wife, unaware of her true identity. We can read this as fate or we can read it as one act of willfulness that leads to another. Oedipus has taken the posture of the Master Player executing terminal moves—but the moves are not terminal. Oedipus is able to bring nothing to an end. Even the act of blinding himself, meant as a kind of concluding gesture, only brings him to a higher vision. What Oedipus sees is not what the gods have done to him, but what he has done. He learns that what had been limited was his vision, and not what he was viewing. His blinding is an unveiling, and like all unveiling it is self-unveiling. Confronted in the end with nothing but his own genius, Oedipus is finally able to touch. The end of his story is a beginning.

俄狄浦斯神话是西方文化宝库中众多伟大的性叙事之一，它巧妙地运用了命运与出身之间戏剧性的关系。俄狄浦斯冲动地杀死了拉伊俄斯，却不知他是自己的亲生父亲。随后，他被野心和欲望驱使，娶了死者的妻子，同样对她的真实身份一无所知。我们可以将其解读为命运的安排，也可以将其解读为一念之差引发另一念之差。俄狄浦斯摆出了大师的姿态，仿佛在进行一场即将结束的表演——但这些表演并非终结。俄狄浦斯无法终结任何事物。即使是刺瞎双眼，看似一种终结的姿态，最终也只是让他获得了更高的境界。俄狄浦斯看到的并非神明加诸于他的，而是他自己所为。他领悟到，真正受限的是他的视野，而非他所看到的。刺瞎双眼是一种揭示，如同所有揭示一样，它也是一种自我揭示。最终，面对的只有他自身的才华，俄狄浦斯终于能够触及内心深处。他的故事的结束，也是新的开始。

What raises this story into the historical is not just that Oedipus sees; it is that we see that he sees. We become listeners who see that we are listening and therefore participating in a now enlarged drama of origins. Nothing is explained here. On the contrary, what we see is that everything remains still to be said.

使这个故事升华为历史的，并非仅仅是俄狄浦斯所见，而是我们看到了他所见。我们成为聆听者，意识到我们正在聆听，因此也参与到这场如今已然扩展的起源戏剧之中。这里没有解释任何事情。相反，我们看到的是，一切仍有待言说。

79

There is a risk here of supposing that because we know our lives to have the character of narrative, we also know what that narrative is. If I were to know the full story of my life I would then have translated it back into explanation. It is as though I could stand as audience to myself, seeing the opening scene and the final scene at the same time, as though I could see my life in its entirety. In doing so I would be performing it, not living it.

这里存在一种风险，即我们因为知道自己的生活具有叙事性，就想当然地认为我们也知道这个叙事是什么。如果我知道我人生的全部故事，我就会把它转化成解释。这就好比我站在自己的视角，同时观看开场和结尾，仿佛我能完整地看到自己的人生。那样的话，我就成了在表演，而不是在生活。

Societal theorists are tempted into the belief that they know the story of a civilization. They can script its final scene of triumph or defeat. It is by way of such end-of-history thinking that the discovered laws of behavior to which persons conform become the scripted laws of behavior to which they must conform.

社会理论家们很容易陷入一种误区，认为自己掌握了一个文明的历史。他们可以预先设定文明最终的胜利或失败。正是通过这种历史终结论的思维方式，人们所遵循的既定行为法则，变成了他们必须遵守的既定行为法则。

True storytellers do not know their own story. What they listen to in their poiesis is the disclosure that wherever there is closure there is the possibility of a new opening, that they do not die at the end, but in the course of play. Neither do they know anyone else’s story in its entirety. The primary work of historians is to open all cultural termini, to reveal continuity where we have assumed something has ended, to remind us that no one’s life, and no culture, can be known, as one would know a poiema, but only learned, as one would learn a poiesis.

真正的故事讲述者并不了解自己的故事。他们在诗意的表达中聆听的是这样的启示：无论何时何地，只要有结束，就蕴藏着新的开始；他们并非在终点消亡，而是在游戏的过程中不断成长。他们也同样无法完全了解他人的故事。历史学家的首要任务是开启所有文化的终点，揭示我们以为已经结束之处的延续性，提醒我们，任何人的生命，任何文化，都无法像了解一个诗篇那样被完全了解，而只能像学习一个诗意的表达那样被学习。

Historians become infinite speakers when they see that whatever begins in freedom cannot end in necessity.

历史学家们一旦意识到，凡是始于自由的事物，都不会以必然告终，他们就成了无穷的演说家。

# ↩

# ↩

80

W E CONTROL NATURE for societal reasons. The control of nature advances with our ability to predict the outcome of natural processes. Inasmuch as predictions are but explanations in reverse, it is possible that they will be quite as combative as explanations. Indeed, prediction is the most highly developed skill of the Master Player, for without it control of an opponent is all the more difficult. It follows that our domination of nature is meant to achieve not certain natural outcomes, but certain societal outcomes.

我们出于社会目的而控制自然。我们对自然的控制随着预测自然进程结果能力的提升而不断进步。由于预测本质上是解释的逆向操作，因此预测本身可能与解释一样具有争议性。事实上，预测是高手最精湛的技能，因为缺乏预测能力，控制对手就更加困难。由此可见，我们对自然的支配并非旨在实现特定的自然结果，而是为了实现特定的社会目标。

A small group of physicists, using calculations of the highest known abstraction, uncovered a predictable sequence of subatomic reactions that led directly to the construction of a thermonuclear bomb. It is true that the successful detonation of the bomb proved the predictions of the physicists, but it is also true that we did not explode the bomb to prove them correct; we exploded it to control the behavior of millions of persons and to bring our relations with them to a certain closure.

一小群物理学家运用当时已知最高抽象程度的计算，揭示了一系列可预测的亚原子反应，这些反应直接导致了热核炸弹的制造。诚然，炸弹的成功引爆证实了物理学家们的预测，但我们引爆炸弹并非为了证明他们的预测正确；我们引爆炸弹是为了控制数百万人的行为，并最终结束我们与他们的关系。

What this example shows is not that we can exercise power over nature, but that our attempt to do so masks our desire for power over each other. This raises a question as to the cultural consequences of abandoning the strategy of power in our attitude toward nature.

这个例子表明的并非我们能够掌控自然，而是我们试图掌控自然的努力掩盖了我们彼此之间权力欲的本质。这就引出了一个问题：如果我们放弃在对待自然的态度中运用权力策略，将会带来怎样的文化后果？

The alternative attitudes toward nature can be characterized in a rough way by saying that the result of approaching nature as a hostile Other whose designs are basically inimical to our interests is the machine, while the result of learning to discipline ourselves to consist with the deepest discernable patterns of natural order is the garden.

对待自然的两种不同态度可以粗略地概括为：将自然视为敌对的“他者”，其设计从根本上与我们的利益相悖，其结果就是机器；而学会约束自己，使其与自然秩序中最深层、最可辨识的模式保持一致，其结果就是花园。

“Machine” is used here as inclusive of technology and not as an example of it—as a way of drawing attention to the mechanical rationality of technology. We might be surprised by the technological devices that spring from the imagination of gifted inventors and engineers, but there is nothing surprising in the technology itself. The physicists’ bomb is as thoroughly mechanical as the Neanderthal’s lever—each the exercise of calculable cause-and-effect sequences.

这里使用“机器”一词，并非特指某种技术，而是指涵盖所有技术——其目的在于强调技术的机械理性。我们或许会对那些出自天才发明家和工程师之手的技术装置感到惊讶，但技术本身却并无任何令人惊讶之处。物理学家制造的炸弹与尼安德特人的杠杆一样，本质上都是机械的——两者都是可计算的因果序列的体现。

“Garden” does not refer to the bounded plot at the edge of the house or the margin of the city. This is not a garden one lives beside, but a garden one lives within. It is a place of growth, of maximized spontaneity. To garden is not to engage in a hobby or an amusement; it is to design a culture capable of adjusting to the widest possible range of surprise in nature. Gardeners are acutely attentive to the deep patterns of natural order, but are also aware that there will always be much lying beyond their vision. Gardening is a horizonal activity.

“花园”并非指房屋边缘或城市边缘那块有边界的地块。它不是与世隔绝的花园，而是我们生活其中的花园。它是生长之地，是最大限度展现自然自发性的地方。园艺并非爱好或消遣，而是构建一种能够适应自然界各种惊喜的文化。园丁们敏锐地关注着自然秩序的深层模式，同时也意识到总有许多事物超越了他们的视野。园艺是一种横向的活动。

Machine and garden are not absolutely opposed to each other. Machinery can exist in the garden quite as finite games can be played within an infinite game. The question is not one of restricting machines from the garden but asking whether a machine serves the interest of the garden, or the garden the interest of the machine. We are familiar with a kind of mechanized gardening that has the appearance of high productivity, but looking closely we can see that what is intended is not the encouragement of natural spontaneity but its harnessing.

机器与花园并非绝对对立。机器可以存在于花园之中，正如有限的游戏可以存在于无限的游戏之中。问题不在于是否应该将机器排除在花园之外，而在于机器是否服务于花园的利益，或者花园是否服务于机器的利益。我们熟悉一种机械化的园艺方式，它表面上效率很高，但仔细观察就会发现，其目的并非鼓励自然的自发性，而是驾驭它。

81

The most elemental difference between the machine and the garden is that one is driven by a force which must be introduced from without, the other grown by an energy which originates from within itself.

机器和花园之间最根本的区别在于，机器是由外部力量驱动的，而花园则是由自身内部产生的能量生长的。

Certainly machines of extraordinary complexity have been built: spacecraft, for example, that sustain themselves for months in the void while performing complicated functions with great accuracy. But no machine has been made, nor can one be made, that has the source of its spontaneity within itself. A machine must be designed, constructed, and fueled.

当然，人类已经制造出极其复杂的机器：例如，能够在太空中持续运行数月并高精度执行复杂功能的航天器。但是，没有任何机器，也不可能制造出自身就具备自发运行的能力。机器必须经过设计、建造和燃料供给。

Certainly gardens can be treated with such a range of chemical and technological strategies that we can speak of “raising” food, and of the food we have raised as “produce.” But no way has been found, or can be found, by which organic growth can be forced from without. The application of fertilizers, herbicides, and any number of other substances does not alter growth but allows growth; it is meant to consist with natural growth. A plant cannot be designed or constructed. Though we seem to give it “fuel” in the form of rich earth and appropriate nutrients, we depend on the plant to make use of the fuel by way of its own vitality. A machine depends on its designer and its operator both for the supply of fuel and its consumption. A machine has not the merest trace of its own spontaneity or vitality. Vitality cannot be given, only found.

当然，我们可以运用各种各样的化学和技术手段来处理花园，以至于我们可以说“种植”食物，并将我们种植的食物称为“农产品”。但是，至今为止，也永远不可能找到任何方法，能够从外部强行促进有机生长。施用化肥、除草剂以及其他各种物质并不会改变植物的生长，而是促进其生长；它的目的是与自然生长相协调。植物无法被设计或建造。尽管我们似乎以肥沃的土壤和适宜的养分的形式为它提供“燃料”，但我们仍然依赖植物凭借自身的活力来利用这些燃料。机器的燃料供应和消耗都依赖于其设计者和操作者。机器本身没有任何自发性或活力。活力无法被赋予，只能被发现。

82

Just as nature has no outside, it has no inside. It is not divided within itself and cannot therefore be used for or against itself. There is no inherent opposition of the living and the nonliving within nature; neither is more or less natural than the other. The use of agricultural poisons, for example, will surely kill selected organisms; it will arrest the spontaneity of living entities—but it is not an unnatural act. Nature has not been changed. All that changes is the way we discipline ourselves to consist with natural order.

正如自然没有外部，它也没有内部。它自身并不分裂，因此既不能利用自身，也不能利用自身。自然界中生物与非生物之间并不存在固有的对立；二者并无孰优孰劣之分。例如，使用农业毒药固然会杀死某些生物；它会抑制生物的自发性——但这并非违背自然的行为。自然本身并未改变。改变的只是我们约束自身以顺应自然秩序的方式。

Our freedom in relation to nature is not the freedom to change nature; it is not the possession of power over natural phenomena. It is the freedom to change ourselves. We are perfectly free to design a culture that will turn on the awareness that vitality cannot be given but only found, that the given patterns of spontaneity in nature are not only to be respected, but to be celebrated.

我们与自然之间的自由并非改变自然的自由，也并非掌控自然现象的权力，而是改变自身的自由。我们完全可以自由地构建一种文化，这种文化将唤醒人们的意识：活力无法被赋予，只能被发现；自然界中既定的自发模式不仅值得尊重，更值得赞颂。

Although “natural order” is the common expression, it has something of a veiling quality about it. More properly speaking, it is not the order of nature but its irreducible spontaneity with which we find ourselves contending. That nature has no outside, and no inside, that it suffers no opposition to itself, that it is not moved by unnatural influence, is not the expression of an order so much as it is the display of a perfect indifference on nature’s part to all matters cultural.

尽管“自然秩序”是常用的说法，但它却带有某种掩盖性的意味。更准确地说，我们所面对的并非自然的秩序，而是其不可化约的自发性。自然既无外在，也无内在，不受自身阻碍，不受人为因素的影响，这与其说是秩序的体现，不如说是自然对一切文化事物漠不关心的表现。

Nature’s source of movement is always from within itself; indeed it is itself. And it is radically distinct from our own source of movement. This is not to say that, possessing no order, nature is chaotic. It is neither chaotic nor ordered. Chaos and order describe the cultural experience of nature—the degree to which nature’s indifferent spontaneity seems to agree with our current manner of cultural self-control. A hurricane, or a plague, or the overpopulation of the earth will seem chaotic to those whose cultural expectations are damaged by them and orderly to those whose expectations have been confirmed by them.

自然界的运动源泉始终源于自身；事实上，它就是自身。这与我们自身的运动源泉截然不同。但这并非意味着，自然界缺乏秩序，因而就是混乱的。它既非混乱，也非有序。混乱与秩序描述的是人们对自然的文化体验——自然界漠然的自发性在多大程度上与我们当下的文化自律方式相契合。飓风、瘟疫或人口过剩，对于那些文化预期受到冲击的人来说，会显得混乱；而对于那些预期得到印证的人来说，则会显得井然有序。

83

The paradox in our relation to nature is that the more deeply a culture respects the indifference of nature, the more creatively it will call upon its own spontaneity in response. The more clearly we remind ourselves that we can have no unnatural influence on nature, the more our culture will embody a freedom to embrace surprise and unpredictability.

我们与自然关系中的悖论在于：一种文化越是尊重自然的无常，就越能创造性地运用自身的自发性来应对自然。我们越是清楚地认识到我们无法对自然施加任何非自然的影响，我们的文化就越能体现出一种拥抱惊喜和不可预测性的自由。

Human freedom is not a freedom over nature; it is the freedom to be natural, that is, to answer to the spontaneity of nature with our own spontaneity. Though we are free to be natural, we are not free by nature; we are free by culture, by history.

人类的自由并非凌驾于自然之上的自由；而是回归自然的自由，也就是说，以我们自身的自发性回应自然的自发性。虽然我们有回归自然的自由，但我们并非天生自由；我们的自由源于文化，源于历史。

The contradiction in our relation to nature is that the more vigorously we attempt to force its agreement with our own designs the more subject we are to its indifference, the more vulnerable to its unseeing forces. The more power we exercise over natural process the more powerless we become before it. In a matter of months we can cut down a rain forest that took tens of thousands of years to grow, but we are helpless in repulsing the desert that takes its place. And the desert, of course, is no less natural than the forest.

我们与自然关系中的矛盾在于：我们越是竭力强迫自然顺应我们的意愿，就越是受制于自然的漠然，越是容易受到其无形力量的影响。我们对自然进程施加的权力越大，在自然面前就越是无能为力。短短几个月，我们就能砍伐一片历经数万年才形成的热带雨林，却无力阻止取而代之的沙漠。而沙漠，当然，也和森林一样，是自然的一部分。

84

Such contradiction is most obvious in the matter of machinery. We make use of machines to increase our power, and therefore our control, over natural phenomena. By exerting themselves no more than is necessary to operate fingertip controls, a team of workers can cut six-lane highways through mountains and dense forest, or fill in wetlands to build shopping malls.

这种矛盾在机械领域体现得最为明显。我们利用机器来增强自身的力量，从而更好地控制自然现象。只需付出操作指尖控制装置所需的最小努力，一群工人就能在山峦和茂密的森林中开辟出六车道高速公路，或者填平湿地建造购物中心。

While a machine greatly aids the operator in such tasks, it also disciplines its operator. As the machine might be considered the extended arms and legs of the worker, the worker might be considered an extension of the machine. All machines, and especially very complicated machines, require operators to place themselves in a provided location and to perform functions mechanically adapted to the functions of the machine. To use the machine for control is to be controlled by the machine.

机器在完成此类任务时固然能极大地帮助操作者，但也对操作者有所约束。机器可以被视为操作者的延伸手臂和腿，而操作者则可以被视为机器的延伸。所有机器，尤其是非常复杂的机器，都要求操作者站在指定位置，执行与机器功能相匹配的机械操作。使用机器进行控制，实际上就是被机器所控制。

To operate a machine one must operate like a machine. Using a machine to do what we cannot do, we find we must do what the machine does.

要操作机器，就必须像机器一样操作。用机器去做我们自己做不到的事，我们就会发现，我们也必须去做机器做的事。

Machines do not, of course, make us into machines when we operate them; we make ourselves into machinery in order to operate them. Machinery does not steal our spontaneity from us; we set it aside ourselves, we deny our originality. There is no style in operating a machine. The more efficient the machine, the more it either limits or absorbs our uniqueness into its operation.

当然，机器并不会让我们在操作它们时变成机器；相反，我们为了操作它们而把自己变成了机器。机器不会夺走我们的自发性；是我们自己放弃了它，否定了我们的独创性。操作机器没有所谓的风格。机器效率越高，它就越会限制或吸收我们的独特性。

Indeed, we come to think that the style of operation does not belong to the operator at all, but is inherent in the machine. Advertisers and manufacturers speak of their products as though they have designed style into them. Most consumer products are “styled” inasmuch as they actually standardize the activity or the taste of the consumer. In a perfect contradiction we are urged to buy a “styled” artifact because others are also buying it—that is, we are asked to express our genius by giving up our genius.

事实上，我们逐渐认为操作风格根本不属于操作者，而是机器本身固有的。广告商和制造商谈论他们的产品时，仿佛风格是他们精心设计的。大多数消费品都带有“风格”，因为它们实际上规范了消费者的行为或品味。这本身就是一个完美的矛盾：我们被敦促购买“风格化”的产品，仅仅因为其他人也在买——也就是说，我们被要求通过放弃自己的天赋来展现自己的才华。

Because we make use of machinery in the belief we can increase the range of our freedom, and instead only decrease it, we use machines against ourselves.

因为我们利用机器的目的是为了扩大自由的范围，但实际上却缩小了自由的范围，所以我们实际上是在利用机器来对付自己。

85

Machinery is contradictory in another way. Just as we use machinery against ourselves, we also use machinery against itself. A machine is not a way of doing something; it stands in the way of doing something.

机器还有另一个矛盾之处。正如我们利用机器来对付自己一样，我们也利用机器来对付它自身。机器本身并非完成某事的方法；它反而阻碍了完成某事。

When we use machines to achieve whatever it is we desire, we cannot have what we desire until we have finished with the machine, until we can rid ourselves of the mechanical means of reaching our intended outcome. The goal of technology is therefore to eliminate itself, to become silent, invisible, carefree.

当我们利用机器来实现我们的愿望时，只有当我们不再依赖机器，摆脱了实现目标的机械手段之后，我们才能真正拥有我们想要的东西。因此，技术的目标是自我消亡，变得悄无声息、隐形无踪、自由自在。

We do not purchase an automobile, for example, merely to own some machinery. Indeed, it is not machinery we are buying at all, but what we can have by way of it: a means of rapidly carrying us from one location to another, an object of envy for others, protection from the weather. Similarly, a radio must cease to exist as equipment and become sound. A perfect radio will draw no attention to itself, will make it seem we are in the very presence of the source of its sound. Neither do we watch a movie screen, nor look at television. We look at what is on television, or in the movie, and become annoyed when the equipment intrudes—when the film is unfocused or the picture tube malfunctions.

例如，我们购买汽车并非仅仅为了拥有一台机器。事实上，我们购买的根本不是机器本身，而是它所能提供的东西：一种快速将我们从一个地方送到另一个地方的工具，一件令人艳羡的物品，以及抵御风雨的庇护。同样，收音机必须不再仅仅是一台机器，而成为声音本身。一台完美的收音机不会引人注目，它会让你感觉仿佛置身于声音的源头。我们观看电影屏幕或电视屏幕，并非仅仅观看电影本身，而是观看电视或电影中的内容，当设备干扰——例如画面模糊或显像管故障——时，我们才会感到恼火。

When machinery functions perfectly it ceases to be there—but so do we. Radios and films allow us to be where we are not and not be where we are. Morever, machinery is veiling. It is a way of hiding our inaction from ourselves under what appear to be actions of great effectiveness. We persuade ourselves that, comfortably seated behind the wheels of our autos, shielded from every unpleasant change of weather, and raising or lowering our foot an inch or two, we have actually traveled somewhere.

当机器运转完美时，它便不再存在——但我们亦然。收音机和电影让我们身处异地，又置身事外。此外，机器具有遮蔽作用。它让我们得以用看似高效的行动掩盖自身的不作为。我们自欺欺人地认为，舒适地坐在汽车驾驶座上，免受任何恶劣天气的影响，只需抬起或放下脚一两英寸，就仿佛已经到达了某个地方。

Such travel is not through space foreign to us, but in a space that belongs to us. We do not move from our point of departure, but with our point of departure. To be moved from our living room by an automobile whose upholstered seats differ scarcely at all from those in our living rooms, to an airport waiting room and then to the airplane where we are provided the same sort of furniture, is to have taken our origin with us; it is to have left home without leaving home. To be at home everywhere is to neutralize space.

这样的旅行并非穿越陌生的空间，而是在我们自身的空间之中。我们并非离开出发点，而是与出发点一同前行。从客厅出发，乘坐一辆座椅与客厅座椅几乎别无二致的汽车，前往机场候机室，再到飞机上，飞机上摆放的家具也与客厅无异，这便是将我们的起点带在身边；这便是离家而不离家。处处皆家的感觉，便是空间的消弭。

Therefore, the importance of reducing time in travel: by arriving as quickly as possible we need not feel as though we had left at all, that neither space nor time can affect us—as though they belong to us, and not we to them.

因此，缩短旅行时间至关重要：通过尽快到达目的地，我们不必感觉自己已经离开，空间和时间都无法影响我们——仿佛它们属于我们，而不是我们属于它们。

We do not go somewhere in a car, but arrive somewhere in a car. Automobiles do not make travel possible, but make it possible for us to move locations without traveling.

我们不是开车去某个地方，而是开车到达某个地方。汽车本身并不能使旅行成为可能，但它使我们能够在不旅行的情况下转换地点。

Thus, the theatricality of machinery: Such movement is but a change of scenes. If effective, the machinery will see to it that we remain untouched by the elements, by other travelers, by those whose towns or lives we are traveling through. We can see without being seen, move without being touched.

因此，机械的戏剧性就在于此：这种移动不过是场景的变换。如果运作得当，这套机械系统将确保我们不受自然环境、其他旅行者以及我们所途经的城镇或居民生活的影响。我们可以视而不见，行而不见。

When most effective, the technology of communication allows us to bring the histories and the experiences of others into our home, but without changing our home. When most effective, the technology of travel allows us to pass through the histories of other persons with the “comforts of home,” but without changing those histories.

通讯技术若能发挥最大效用，便能让我们把别人的历史和经历带入自己的家中，而无需改变自己的家。旅行技术若能发挥最大效用，便能让我们带着“家的舒适”体验他人的历史，而无需改变这些历史本身。

When it is most effective, machinery will have no effect at all.

当机械设备发挥最大效用时，它将完全不起作用。

86

In still another way is machinery contradictory. Using it against itself and against ourselves, we also use machinery against each other.

机器本身也具有矛盾性。我们既利用机器对抗自身，也利用机器对抗人类，同样，我们也利用机器对抗彼此。

I cannot use machinery without using it with another. I do not talk on the telephone; I talk with someone on the telephone. I listen to someone on the radio, drive to visit a friend, compute business transactions. To the degree that my association with you depends on such machinery, the connecting medium makes each of us an extension of itself. If your business activities cannot translate into data recognizable by my computer, I can have no business with you. If you do not live where I can drive to see you, I will find another friend. In each case your relationship to me does not depend on my needs but on the needs of my machinery.

我无法脱离其他机器单独使用。我不打电话说话，而是和别人打电话。我听广播，开车去看望朋友，处理商业交易。我与你的联系在某种程度上依赖于这种机器，连接媒介使我们彼此成为机器自身的延伸。如果你的商业活动无法转化为我的电脑可识别的数据，我们就无法与你开展业务。如果你住的地方我无法开车去看望，我会另寻朋友。在每一种情况下，你与我的关系都不取决于我的需求，而是取决于我的机器的需求。

If to operate a machine is to operate like a machine, then we not only operate with each other like machines, we operate each other like machines. And if a machine is most effective when it has no effect, then we operate each other in such a way that we reach the outcome desired—in such a way that nothing happens.

如果操作机器就是像机器一样操作，那么我们不仅像机器一样彼此协作，而且像机器一样互相操控。如果机器最有效的时候就是它什么都不产生，那么我们互相操控的方式就是以达到预期结果的方式——什么都不发生。

The inherent hostility of machine-mediated relatedness is nowhere more evident than in the use of the most theatrical machines of all: instruments of war. All weapons are designed to affect others without affecting ourselves, to make others answerable to the technology in our control. Weapons are the equipment of finite games designed in such a way that they do not maximize the play but eliminate it. Weapons are meant not to win contests but to end them. Killers are not victors; they are unopposed competitors, players without a game, living contradictions.

机器媒介关系中固有的敌意，在战争工具——所有机器中最具戏剧性的工具——的使用中体现得最为明显。所有武器的设计目的都是为了影响他人而不影响自身，使他人服从于我们掌控的技术。武器是有限博弈的装备，其设计目的并非最大化博弈，而是终结博弈。武器的目的不是为了赢得竞争，而是为了终结竞争。杀戮者并非胜利者；他们是无人对抗的竞争者，是无规则的玩家，是活生生的矛盾体。

This is particularly the case with the airborne electronic weaponry of the present century, where the operator deals only with the technology—buttons, blips, lights, dials, levers, computer data—and never with the unseen opponent. Indeed, so empty of drama is the modern machinery of slaughter that it is intended to assault enemies only while they are still unseen. This reaches an extreme form in the belief that our enemies are not unseen because they are enemies, but are enemies because they are unseen.

本世纪的机载电子武器尤其如此，操作人员只需与技术打交道——按钮、信号、指示灯、旋钮、操纵杆、计算机数据——而无需面对看不见的敌人。事实上，现代杀戮机器如此缺乏戏剧性，以至于它的目的仅仅是在敌人尚未被发现时发动攻击。这种观念走向极端，以至于人们认为敌人之所以看不见，并非因为他们是敌人，而是因为他们看不见，所以才成为敌人。

There is a logic in the instrumentality of death that leads us to killing the unseen because they are unseen. The crudest spear or sword is raised by an attacker because the independent existence of another cannot be countenanced— because the other cannot be seen as an other. Just as I insist that the condition of our friendship is your unresisting use of the telephone, I will expect the weapon in my hand to function without finding an other that can resist it. Killers can suffer no suggestion that they are living into the open, that their histories are not finished, that their freedom is always a freedom with others, and not over others, that it is not their vision that is limited but what they are viewing.

死亡的工具性逻辑驱使我们去杀害那些看不见的人，因为他们看不见。攻击者之所以会举起最原始的长矛或刀剑，是因为他们无法容忍他人的独立存在——因为他们无法将他人视为“他者”。正如我坚持认为我们友谊的前提是你无条件地使用电话一样，我也期望我手中的武器无需找到任何可以抵抗它的人就能发挥作用。杀人者无法接受任何暗示，比如他们生活在公开场合，他们的历史尚未终结，他们的自由始终是与他人共存的自由，而非凌驾于他人之上的自由，受限的不是他们的视野，而是他们所看到的东西。

The fact that the technology of slaughter at vast distances has become extremely sophisticated does not culturally advance its highly trained operators over club-swinging primitives; it makes complete the blindness that was but rudimentary in the primitive. It is the supreme triumph of resentment over vision. We are the unseeing killing the unseen.

远距离屠杀技术的日臻完善，并未使训练有素的操作者在文化上超越挥舞棍棒的原始人；反而使原始人原本就存在的盲目更加彻底。这是怨恨战胜了洞察力，是最终的胜利。我们是看不见的杀戮者，而我们却看不见。

Not everyone who uses machinery is a killer. But when the use of machinery springs from our attempt to respond to the indifference of nature with an indifference of our own to nature, we have begun to acquire the very indifference to persons that has led to the century’s grandest crimes by its most civilized nations.

并非所有使用机器的人都是杀人犯。但是，当我们试图用对自然的漠视来回应自然的漠视时，我们就开始变得对人漠不关心，而这种漠视正是导致本世纪最文明国家犯下滔天罪行的原因。

87

If indifference to nature leads to the machine, the indifference of nature leads to the garden. All culture has the form of gardening: the encouragement of spontaneity in others by way of one’s own, the respect for source, and the refusal to convert source into resource.

如果说对自然的漠视导致了机器的出现，那么对自然的漠视则导致了花园的诞生。所有文化都具有园艺的形式：通过自身的自发性来鼓励他人的自发性，尊重自然之源，并拒绝将自然之源转化为资源。

Gardeners slaughter no animals. They kill nothing. Fruits, seeds, vegetables, nuts, grains, grasses, roots, flowers, herbs, berries—all are collected when they have ripened, and when their collection is in the interest of the garden’s heightened and continued vitality. Harvesting respects a source, leaves it unexploited, suffers it to be as it is.

园丁不宰杀任何动物，也不杀害任何生命。水果、种子、蔬菜、坚果、谷物、草、根茎、花卉、香草、浆果——所有这些都在成熟时采摘，并且只有在有利于花园持续繁荣发展的情况下才会采摘。采摘是对资源的尊重，不加过度开发，任其保持原貌。

Animals cannot be harvested. They mature, but they do not “ripen.” They are killed not when they have completed the cycle of their vitality but when they are at the peak of their vitality. Finite gardeners, converting agriculture into commerce, “raise” or “produce” animals—or meat products—as though by machine. Animal husbandry is a science, a method of controlling growth. It assumes that animals belong to us. What is source in them is to be resource for us. Cattle are confined to pens to prevent such movement as would “toughen” their flesh. Geese, their feet nailed to the floor, are force fed like machines until they can be butchered for their fattened livers.

动物无法被“收割”。它们会成熟，但并非“成熟”。它们并非在完成生命周期后被宰杀，而是在生命力达到顶峰时被宰杀。那些将农业转化为商业的“有限的园丁”们，如同机器一般“饲养”或“生产”动物——或肉类产品。畜牧业是一门科学，一种控制增长的方法。它假定动物属于我们。它们身上的源泉将成为我们的资源。牛被圈养在牛栏里，以防止任何可能使它们肉质“变硬”的活动。鹅的蹄子被钉在地上，像机器一样被强制喂食，直到它们可以被屠宰，取走肥美的肝脏。

While machinery is meant to work changes without changing its operators, gardening transforms its workers. One learns how to drive a car, one learns to drive as a car; but one becomes a gardener.

机器运转的目的是在不改变操作人员的情况下完成各种变化，而园艺则会改变园艺者本身。一个人学习驾驶汽车，是学会像汽车一样驾驶；但成为一名园丁，则意味着成为一名真正的园丁。

Gardening is not outcome-oriented. A successful harvest is not the end of a garden’s existence, but only a phase of it. As any gardener knows, the vitality of a garden does not end with a harvest. It simply takes another form. Gardens do not “die” in the winter but quietly prepare for another season.

园艺并非以结果为导向。丰收并非花园存在的终点，而只是其生命周期中的一个阶段。正如任何园丁所知，花园的生命力并不会随着收获而消逝，它只是以另一种形式延续下去。花园不会在冬季“枯萎”，而是静静地为下一个季节做好准备。

Gardeners celebrate variety, unlikeness, spontaneity. They understand that an abundance of styles is in the interest of vitality. The more complex the organic content of the soil, for example—that is, the more numerous its sources of change—the more vigorous its liveliness. Growth promotes growth.

园丁们崇尚多样性、独特性和自然生长。他们明白，丰富的风格有利于植物的活力。例如，土壤的有机成分越复杂——也就是说，土壤的变化来源越多——植物的生命力就越旺盛。生长促进生长。

So also in culture. Infinite players understand that the vigor of a culture has to do with the variety of its sources, the differences within itself. The unique and the surprising are not suppressed in some persons for the strength of others. The genius in you stimulates the genius in me.

文化亦是如此。博学之士深谙，文化的活力源于其来源的多样性，源于其内部的差异。独特与惊艳之处并不会因他人的强势而被压制。你的天赋激发了我的天赋。

One operates a machine effectively, so that it disappears, giving way to results in which the machine has no part. One gardens creatively, so that all the sources of the garden’s vitality appear in its harvest, giving rise to a continuity in which we take an active part.

高效操作机器，使其悄然消失，最终的结果与机器无关。创造性地耕耘花园，使花园所有的生命力都体现在收获之中，从而形成一种我们积极参与其中的延续性。

88

Inasmuch as gardens do not conclude with a harvest and are not played for a certain outcome, one never arrives anywhere with a garden.

由于花园不会以收获告终，也不是为了达到某种特定结果而存在的，所以拥有花园的人永远不会到达任何地方。

A garden is a place where growth is found. It has its own source of change. One does not bring change to a garden, but comes to a garden prepared for change, and therefore prepared to change. It is possible to deal with growth only out of growth. True parents do not see to it that their children grow in a particular way, according to a preferred pattern or scripted stages, but they see to it that they grow with their children. The character of one’s parenting, if it is genuinely dramatic, must be constantly altered from within as the children change from within. So, too, with teaching, or working with, or loving each other.

花园是孕育成长的地方，它拥有自身变化的源泉。人们并非强行改变花园，而是带着对变化的准备来到花园，并因此做好了迎接变化的准备。唯有在成长中，才能更好地应对成长。真正的父母不会强迫孩子按照某种既定的模式或阶段成长，而是与孩子一同成长。如果父母的教养方式真正具有戏剧性，那么随着孩子内在的变化，父母自身也必须不断调整。教导、共事、彼此相爱，亦是如此。

It is in the garden that we discover what travel truly is. We do not journey to a garden but by way of it.

正是在花园里，我们才能发现旅行的真谛。我们不是前往花园，而是穿过花园。

Genuine travel has no destination. Travelers do not go somewhere, but constantly discover they are somewhere else.
