Since gardening is a way not of subduing the indifference of nature but of raising one’s own spontaneity to respond to the disregarding vagaries and unpredictabilities of nature, we do not look on nature as a sequence of changing scenes but look on ourselves as persons in passage.

真正的旅行没有目的地。旅行者并非前往某处，而是不断发现自己身处别处。园艺并非征服自然的冷漠，而是提升自身的自发性，以应对自然无情的变幻莫测，因此，我们并非将自然视为一系列不断变化的场景，而是将自身视为行者。

Nature does not change; it has no inside or outside. It is therefore not possible to travel through it. All travel is therefore change within the traveler, and it is for that reason that travelers are always somewhere else. To travel is to grow.

自然本身并无变化；它没有内外之分。因此，我们无法穿越自然。所有的旅行，都是旅行者内在的改变，也正因如此，旅行者总是身处他乡。旅行即成长。

Genuine travelers travel not to overcome distance but to discover distance. It is not distance that makes travel necessary, but travel that makes distance possible. Distance is not determined by the measurable length between objects, but by the actual differences between them. The motels around the airports in Chicago and Atlanta are so little different from the motels around the airports of Tokyo and Frankfurt that all essential distances dissolve in likeness. What is truly separated is distinct; it is unlike. “The only true voyage would be not to travel through a hundred different lands with the same pair of eyes, but to see the same land through a hundred different pairs of eyes” (Proust).

真正的旅行者旅行不是为了克服距离，而是为了发现距离。并非距离使旅行成为必要，而是旅行使距离成为可能。距离并非由物体之间可测量的长度决定，而是由它们之间的实际差异决定。芝加哥和亚特兰大机场附近的汽车旅馆与东京和法兰克福机场附近的汽车旅馆几乎没有什么区别，以至于所有本质的距离都消融在相似之中。真正分离的是截然不同的事物；是迥然不同的事物。“真正的旅行不是用同一双眼睛游历一百个不同的国家，而是用一百双不同的眼睛去看同一个国家”（普鲁斯特）。

A gardener, whose attention is ever on the spontaneities of nature, acquires the gift of seeing differences, looks always for the merest changes in plant growth, or in the composition of the soil, the emerging populations of insects and earthworms. So will gardeners, as parents, see changes of the smallest subtlety in their children, or as teachers see the signs of an increasing skill, and possibly wisdom, in their students. A garden, a family, a classroom—any place of human gathering whatsoever—will offer no end of variations to be observed, each an arrow pointing toward yet more changes. But these observed changes are not theatrically amusing to genuine gardeners; they dramatically open themselves to a renewed future.

一位园丁，如果时刻关注自然界的自发变化，便能培养出洞察差异的天赋，时刻留意植物生长、土壤成分、昆虫和蚯蚓种群的细微变化。园丁如同父母，能够察觉孩子身上最细微的变化；如同教师，能够发现学生技能乃至智慧的提升。花园、家庭、教室——任何人类聚集的场所——都蕴藏着无穷无尽的变化，每一种变化都指向更多的未来。但对于真正的园丁而言，这些观察到的变化并非滑稽可笑，而是为崭新的未来开启了一扇大门。

So, too, with those who look everywhere for difference, who see the earth as source, who celebrate the genius in others, who are not prepared against but for surprise. “I have traveled far in Concord” (Thoreau).

同样，那些处处寻求差异、视大地为源泉、赞美他人才华、不防备惊喜反而欣然接受惊喜的人也是如此。“我在康科德走了很远的路”（梭罗）。

89

Since machinery requires force from without, its use always requires a search for consumable power. When we think of nature as resource, it is as a resource for power. As we preoccupy ourselves with machinery, nature is increasingly thought of as a reservoir of needed substances. It is a quantity of materials that exist to be consumed, chiefly in our machines.

由于机械运转需要外部动力，因此其使用始终需要对可消耗的能源进行渴求。当我们把自然视为资源时，它实际上是一种能源。随着我们对机械的日益关注，自然也越来越被视为所需物质的储藏库。它是一种可供消耗的物质，主要用于我们的机器运转。

Being undivided, nature cannot be used against itself. We do not therefore consume it , or exhaust it We simply rearrange our societal patterns in a way that reduces our ability to respond creatively to the existing patterns of spontaneity. That is, to use the societal expression, we create waste. Waste, of course, is by no means unnatural. The trash and garbage of a civilization do not befoul nature; they are nature—but in a form society no longer is able to exploit for its own ends.

自然作为一个整体，不可分割，因此无法被利用。所以我们既不消耗自然，也不耗尽自然。我们只是重新调整了社会模式，从而削弱了我们对现有自发模式进行创造性反应的能力。也就是说，用通俗的话来说，我们制造了废物。当然，废物本身并非不自然。文明的垃圾和废弃物并非玷污自然；它们本身就是自然——只不过是以一种社会无法再为自身利益加以利用的形式存在。

Society regards its waste as an unfortunate, but necessary, consequence of its activities—what is left when we have made essential societal goods available. But waste is not the result of what we have made. It is what we have made. Waste plutonium is not an indirect consequence of the nuclear industry; it is a product of that industry.

社会将废弃物视为自身活动带来的不幸却又不可避免的后果——是我们在提供必要的社会产品后所剩下的东西。但废弃物并非我们制造的结果，它本身就是我们制造的东西。钚废料并非核工业的间接后果，而是该工业的产物。

90

Waste is unveiling. As we find ourselves standing in garbage that we know is our own, we find also that it is garbage we have chosen to make, and having chosen to make it could choose not to make it. Because waste is unveiling, we remove it. We place it where it is out of sight. We either find uninhabited areas where waste can be disposed of, or fill them with our refuse until they become uninhabitable. Since a flourishing society will vigorously exploit its natural resources, it will produce correspondingly great quantities of trash, and quickly its uninhabited lands will overflow with waste, threatening to make the society’s own habitation into a wasteland.

垃圾是一种揭示。当我们发现自己身处垃圾之中，而这些垃圾明明是我们自己制造的，我们也意识到，这些垃圾是我们自己选择的。既然选择了制造，我们本可以选择不制造。因为垃圾是一种揭示，所以我们清除它，把它放到看不见的地方。我们要么找到无人居住的地区倾倒垃圾，要么用垃圾填满这些地区，直到它们变得不适宜居住。一个繁荣的社会会大力开发其自然资源，因此也会产生相应的巨量垃圾，很快，无人居住的土地就会被垃圾淹没，甚至有可能将社会自身的居住地变成一片荒地。

Because waste is unveiling, it is not only placed out of sight, it is declared a kind of antiproperty. No one owns it. Part of the contradiction in the phenomenon of waste is that treating nature as though it belongs to us we must soon treat nature as though it belongs to no one. Not only does no one own waste, no one wants it. Instead of competing to possess these particular products, we compete to dispossess them. We force it on others less able to rid themselves of it. Trash accumulates in slums, sewage runs downstream, airborne acid drifts hundreds of miles settling on the lands of those powerless to halt its “disposal” into the atmosphere. Thousands of square miles of farm lands have been laid waste by the construction of multilane highways, or submerged by dams whose water is used to flush waste from distant cities.

因为废弃物具有揭示本质的作用，它不仅被放置在视线之外，更被视为一种反财产。它不属于任何人。废弃物现象的矛盾之处在于，如果我们把自然当作属于我们的财产来对待，那么我们很快就会把自然当作不属于任何人的财产来对待。不仅无人拥有废弃物，也无人想要它。我们不再争夺这些特定产品的所有权，而是争夺对它们的占有。我们强迫那些更无力摆脱它们的人承担这些负担。垃圾堆积在贫民窟，污水顺流而下，空气中的酸性物质漂移数百英里，最终落在那些无力阻止其“排放”到大气中的人们的土地上。数千平方英里的农田因修建多车道高速公路而荒废，或被水坝淹没，而水坝的水被用来冲刷来自远方城市的污水。

Waste is the antiproperty that becomes the possession of losers. It is the emblem of the untitled.

废弃物是失败者的反财产，是无主之物的象征。

Waste is unveiling, because it persists in showing itself as waste, and as our waste. If waste is the result of our indifference to nature, it is also the way we experience the indifference of nature. Waste is therefore a reminder that society is a species of culture. Looking about at the wasteland into which we have converted our habitation, we can plainly see that nature is not whatever we want it to be; but we can also plainly see that society is only what we want it to be.

浪费是一种揭示，因为它不断地以浪费的形式出现，而且是我们造成的浪费。如果说浪费是我们对自然漠不关心的结果，那么它也是我们体验自然漠不关心的方式。因此，浪费提醒我们，社会是一种文化。环顾我们把家园变成的荒芜之地，我们可以清楚地看到，自然并非我们想要的样子；但我们也可以清楚地看到，社会也只是我们想要的样子。

It is a consequence of this contradiction that the more waste a society produces, the more unveiling that waste is, and thus the more vigorously must a society deny that it produces any waste at all; the more it must dispose, or hide, or ignore, its detritus.

这种矛盾导致一个社会产生的垃圾越多，这些垃圾就越容易被揭露，因此，一个社会就越要极力否认自己产生任何垃圾；就越要处理、隐藏或忽视自己的垃圾。

91

Since the attempt to control nature is at its heart the attempt to control other persons, we can expect societies to be less patient with those cultures which express some degree of indifference to societal goals and values. It is this repeated parallel that brings us to see that the society that creates natural waste creates human waste.

既然试图控制自然的本质是试图控制他人，那么我们可以预料到，社会对那些对社会目标和价值观表现出一定程度漠不关心的文化，会更加缺乏耐心。正是这种反复出现的类比，让我们看到，制造自然废物的社会，也会产生人类的废物。

Waste persons are those no longer useful as resources to a society for whatever reason, and have become apatrides, or noncitizens. Waste persons must be placed out of view—in ghettos, slums, reservations, camps, retirement villages, mass graves, remote territories, strategic hamlets—all places of desolation, and uninhabitable. We live in a century whose Master Players have created many millions of such “superfluous persons” (Rubenstein).

“废物”指的是那些因各种原因不再对社会有利用价值，沦为无国籍人士或非公民的人。必须将他们安置在无人问津的地方——贫民窟、棚户区、保留地、营地、养老院、万人坑、偏远地区、战略要地——所有这些荒凉且不适宜居住的地方。我们生活在一个“幕后操纵者”制造了数百万此类“多余之人”（鲁宾斯坦语）的世纪。

A people does not become superfluous by itself, any more than natural waste creates itself. It is society that declares some persons to be waste. Human trash is not an unfortunate burden on a society, an indirect result of its proper conduct; it is its direct product. European settlers in the American, African, and Asian continents did not happen to come upon populations of unwanted persons nature had thrust in their way; they made them superfluous by way of some of the most important and irreversible principles of their societies.

一个民族不会自行变得多余，正如自然界的废物不会自行产生一样。是社会将某些人视为废物。人类的“垃圾”并非社会不幸的负担，也不是其良好行为的间接结果；它是社会行为的直接产物。欧洲殖民者在美洲、非洲和亚洲大陆并非偶然遇到自然界强加给他们的不受欢迎的人群；而是他们通过自身社会中一些最重要且不可逆转的原则，使这些人变得多余。

Strictly speaking, waste persons do not exist outside the boundaries of a society. They are not society’s enemies. One does not go to war against them, as one goes to war against another society. Waste persons do not constitute an alternative or threatening society; they constitute an unveiling culture. They are therefore “purged.” A society cleanses itself of them.

严格来说，社会渣滓并非存在于社会之外。他们并非社会的敌人。人们不会像对待其他社会那样对他们发动战争。社会渣滓并不构成另一种社会或威胁；他们构成了一种揭露社会弊端的文化。因此，他们被“清除”。社会会清除他们。

92

When society is unveiled, when we see that it is whatever we want it to be, that it is a species of culture with nothing necessary in it, by no means a phenomenon of nature or a manifestation of instinct, nature is no longer shaped and fitted into one or another set of societal goals. Unveiled, we stand before a nature whose only face is its hidden self-origination: its genius.

当社会被揭开面纱，当我们看清它其实是我们想要它成为的样子，看清它不过是一种文化，其中并无任何必然性，绝非自然现象或本能的体现，自然便不再受制于任何特定的社会目标。揭开面纱后，我们面对的自然，其唯一的面貌便是它隐秘的自我起源：它的天赋。

We see nature as genius when we see as genius.

当我们把自然视为天才时，我们也会把自然视为天才。

We understand nature as source when we understand ourselves as source. We abandon all attempts at an explanation of nature when we see that we cannot be explained, when our own self-origination cannot be stated as fact. We behold the irreducible otherness of nature when we behold ourselves as its other.

当我们认识到自身即是源泉时，我们便能理解自然是源泉。当我们意识到自身无法被解释，当我们自身的起源无法被陈述为事实时，我们便会放弃一切解释自然的尝试。当我们视自身为自然的他者时，我们便能洞悉自然那不可化约的他者性。

93

For the infinite player, seeing as genius, nature is the absolutely unlike. The infinite player recognizes nothing on the face of nature. Nature displays not only its indifference to human existence but its difference as well.

对于无限的玩家而言，自然被视为天才，与他截然不同。无限的玩家对自然表面的一切视而不见。自然不仅展现出对人类存在的漠然，也展现出与人类的差异。

Nature offers no home. Although we become gardeners in response to its indifference, nature does nothing of itself to feed us. In Jewish and Islamic mythology God provided us with a garden but did not, indeed could not, do the gardening for us. It was only a garden because we could respond to it, because we could be responsible for it. Our responsibility lay in noting its variabilities and discrete features. We were to name the animals, separating one from the other. This garden was not a machine-like device automatically providing food for us. Neither were we machine-like, driven from without and destined from within. According to this myth, God did breathe life into us, but in order to continue living we had to do our own breathing.

大自然不提供家园。尽管我们因大自然的冷漠而成为园丁，但大自然本身并不会主动养活我们。在犹太教和伊斯兰教的神话中，上帝赐予我们一座花园，但他并没有，也根本无法替我们耕耘。它之所以成为花园，是因为我们能够回应它，因为我们能够对它负责。我们的责任在于观察它的变迁和独特之处。我们要给动物命名，将它们区分开来。这座花园并非一台自动为我们提供食物的机器。我们也不是机器，并非受外力驱使，也并非由内而外决定。根据这个神话，上帝确实赋予了我们生命，但为了延续生命，我们必须自己呼吸。

But responsibility for the garden does not mean that we can make a garden of nature, as though it were a poiema of which we could take possession. A garden is not something we have, over which we stand as gods. A garden is a poiesis, a receptivity to variety, a vision of differences that leads always to a making of differences. The poet joyously suffers the unlike, reduces nothing, explains nothing, possesses nothing.

但对花园的责任并不意味着我们可以将自然变成花园，仿佛它是一个我们可以占有的诗篇。花园并非我们所拥有的，我们也不是凌驾于其上的神明。花园是一种诗意，一种对多样性的接纳，一种对差异的洞察，而这种洞察总是导向差异的创造。诗人欣然接受差异，不简化任何事物，不解释任何事物，也不占有任何事物。

We stand before genius in silence. We cannot speak it, we can only speak as it. Yet, though I speak as genius, I cannot speak for genius. I cannot give nature a voice in my script. I can not give others a voice in my script—without denying their own source, their originality. To do so is to cease responding to the other, to cease being responsible. No one and nothing belong in my script.

我们默默地站在天才面前。我们无法言说天才，只能以天才的身份去表达。然而，即便我以天才的身份发言，我也无法代表天才发言。我无法在我的剧本中赋予自然以声音。我无法在我的剧本中赋予他人以声音——除非我否定他们的源泉和独创性。那样做，就等于停止回应他人，停止承担责任。任何人和事都不属于我的剧本。

The homelessness of nature, its utter indifference to human existence, disclose to the infinite player that nature is the genius of the dramatic.

大自然的无家可归，它对人类生存的漠不关心，向无限的表演者揭示了大自然是戏剧的天才。

# ↩

# ↩

94

M YTH PROVOKES Explanation but accepts none of it. Where explanation absorbs the unspeakable into the speakable, myth reintroduces the silence that makes original discourse possible.

神话激发解释，却不接受任何解释。解释将不可言说之物纳入可言说之物，而神话则重新引入沉默，使最初的论述成为可能。

Explanations establish islands, even continents, of order and predictability. But these regions were first charted by adventurers whose lives are narratives of exploration and risk. They found them only by mythic journeys into the wayless open. When the less adventuresome settlers arrive later to work out the details and domesticate these spaces, they easily lose the sense that all this firm knowledge does not expunge myth, but floats in it.

解释构建出秩序与可预测的岛屿，甚至是大陆。但这些区域最初是由那些人生本身就是探索与冒险故事的冒险家们绘制的。他们只能通过神话般的旅程，深入到茫茫无际的荒野才能找到它们。当那些不那么冒险的定居者后来来到这里，着手处理细节并驯服这些地方时，他们很容易忘记，所有这些确凿的知识并不能消除神话，反而会漂浮在神话之中。

Few discoveries were greater than Copernicus’, for they projected an order into the heavens that no one has successfully challenged. Many thought then, and some still think, that this great statement of truth dispelled clouds of myth that had kept humankind in retarding darkness. What Copernicus dispelled, however, were not myths but other explanations. Myths lie elsewhere. To see where, we do not look at the facts in Copernicus’ works; we look for the story in his stating them. Knowledge is what successful explanation has led to; the thinking that sent us forth, however, is pure story.

很少有发现能超越哥白尼的发现，因为他向苍穹投射出一种至今无人能撼动的秩序。当时许多人认为，现在也有人这样认为，这一伟大的真理宣告驱散了笼罩人类的迷雾，使人类摆脱了停滞不前的黑暗。然而，哥白尼驱散的并非迷雾，而是其他的解释。迷雾存在于别处。要探寻迷雾的所在，我们不能只看哥白尼著作中的事实，而应该探究他阐述这些事实背后的故事。知识是成功解释所带来的结果；然而，引领我们走向未来的思维方式，却纯粹是一种故事。

Copernicus was a traveler who went with a hundred pairs of eyes, daring to look again at all that is familiar in the hope of vision. What we hear in this account is the ancient saga of the solitary wanderer, the peregrinus, who risks anything for the sake of surprise. True, at a certain point he stopped to look and may have ended his journey as a Master Player setting down bounded fact. But what resounds most deeply in the life of Copernicus is the journey that made knowledge possible and not the knowledge that made the journey successful.

哥白尼是一位拥有百双眼睛的旅行者，他敢于重新审视一切熟悉的事物，渴望获得新的启示。我们从这段记载中听到的，是古老孤独的游子——“peregrinus”（游方僧）的传奇故事，他为了追求惊喜而甘愿冒险。诚然，他曾在某个时刻停下来仔细观察，或许最终以一位大师的身份结束了旅程，记录下了一些确凿的事实。但哥白尼一生中最令人铭记的，并非使旅程成功的知识本身，而是他创造知识的旅程。

That myth does not accept the explanations it provokes we can see in the boldness with which thinkers in any territorial endeavor reexamine the familiar for a higher seeing. Indeed, the very liveliness of a culture is determined not by how frequently these thinkers discover new continents of knowledge but by how frequently they depart to seek them.

这种迷思无法接受它所引发的解释，而我们可以从思想家们在任何领域探索中，以大胆的姿态重新审视熟悉的事物，从而获得更高层次的理解这一点中看出。事实上，一种文化的活力并非取决于这些思想家发现新知识领域的频率，而是取决于他们探索新知识领域的频率。

A culture can be no stronger than its strongest myths.

一种文化的强大程度取决于其最强大的神话。

95

A story attains the status of myth when it is retold, and persistently retold, solely for its own sake.

当一个故事被反复讲述，仅仅为了讲述而讲述时，它就获得了神话的地位。

If I tell a story as a way of bracing up an argument or amusing an audience, I am not telling it for its own sake. To tell a story for its own sake is to tell it for no other reason than that it is a story. Great stories have this feature: To listen to them and learn them is to become their narrators.

如果我讲故事是为了增强论点或逗乐听众，那我就不是在为故事本身而讲故事。真正为故事本身而讲故事，就是仅仅因为它是故事而讲故事。伟大的故事都具有这样的特点：聆听和学习它们，就如同成为了它们的讲述者。

Our first response to hearing a story is the desire to tell it ourselves—the greater the story the greater the desire. We will go to considerable time and inconvenience to arrange a situation for its retelling. It is as though the story is itself seeking the occasion for its recurrence, making use of us as its agents. We do not go out searching for stories for ourselves; it is rather the stories that have found us for themselves.

我们听到故事后的第一反应就是想要亲自讲述——故事越精彩，这种渴望就越强烈。我们会花费大量时间和精力，费尽心思安排合适的场合来重述这个故事。仿佛故事本身也在寻找重现的机会，而我们则成为了它的媒介。我们并非主动去寻找故事，而是故事主动找到了我们。

Great stories cannot be observed, any more than an infinite game can have an audience. Once I hear the story I enter into its own dimensionality. I inhabit its space at its time. I do not therefore understand the story in terms of my experience, but my experience in terms of the story. Stories that have the enduring strength of myths reach through experience to touch the genius in each of us. But experience is the result of this generative touch, not its cause. So far is this the case that we can even say that if we cannot tell a story about what happened to us, nothing has happened to us.

伟大的故事无法被观察，正如一场无限的游戏无法拥有观众。一旦我聆听了故事，我就进入了它自身的维度。我置身于它的时间和空间。因此，我并非用我的经验去理解故事，而是用故事去理解我的经验。那些拥有神话般永恒力量的故事，能够穿透经验，触动我们每个人内心深处的天赋。但经验是这种创造性触动的结果，而非其原因。正因如此，我们甚至可以说，如果我们无法讲述发生在我们身上的故事，那么我们身上就什么也没发生过。

It was not Freud’s theory of the unconscious that led him to Oedipus, but the myth of Oedipus that shaped the way he listened to his patients. “The theory of instincts,” he wrote, “is so to say our mythology.” So too, then, the theory of the unconscious that follows from it, and the superego, and the ego. This is a mythology of such poetic strength that it has altered not only the way we understand our experience, but our experience itself. Who of us has not known a crisis of ego, the disturbing presence of unwanted feelings, or the anxious recoil from a more polymorphously embodied sexuality? These experiences are not described by Freud the dispassionate scientist; they are made possible by Freud the mythic dreamer.

并非弗洛伊德的无意识理论引领他走向俄狄浦斯，而是俄狄浦斯神话塑造了他倾听病人的方式。“本能理论，”他写道，“可以说是我们的神话。”由此衍生的无意识理论、超我以及自我，亦是如此。这是一种极具诗意力量的神话，它不仅改变了我们理解自身经验的方式，也改变了我们经验本身。我们当中谁不曾经历过自我危机、不想要的感受带来的困扰，或是面对更加多元化的性欲时产生的焦虑退缩？这些经验并非由冷静的科学家弗洛伊德描述；它们是由充满神话色彩的梦想家弗洛伊德创造的。

As myths make individual experience possible, they also make collective experience possible. Whole civilizations rise from stories—and can rise from nothing else. It is not the historical experience of Jews that makes the Torah meaningful. The Torah is no more a description of the creation of the earth and early Jewish life than the theory of instincts is a description of the psyches of a handful of bourgeois Viennese of the early twentieth century. The Torah is not the story of the Jews; it is what makes Judaism a story.

神话使个体经验成为可能，也使集体经验成为可能。整个文明都源于故事——也只能源于故事。赋予《托拉》意义的并非犹太人的历史经验。《托拉》并非对地球创造和早期犹太人生活的描述，正如本能理论并非对二十世纪初少数维也纳资产阶级人士心理的描述一样。《托拉》并非犹太人的故事；它使犹太教成为一个故事。

We tell myths for their own sake, because they are stories that insist on being stories—and insist on being told. We come to life at their touch.

我们讲述神话，是为了神话本身，因为它们是执意要成为故事，执意要被讲述的故事。我们因它们的触动而获得生命。

However seriously we might regard them as so much inert poiema, and attach metaphysical meanings to them, they spring back out of their own vitality. When we look into a story to find its meaning, it is always a meaning we have brought with us to look at.

然而，无论我们如何严肃地将它们视为毫无生气的诗歌，并赋予它们形而上学的意义，它们都会从自身的生命力中重新焕发活力。当我们探究一个故事的意义时，我们所探寻的总是我们自身携带的意义。

Myths are like magic trees in the garden of culture. They do not grow on but out of the silent earth of nature. The more we strip these trees of their fruit or prune them back to our favored design, the more imposing and fecund they become.

神话就像文化花园里的魔法树。它们并非生长于自然静谧的土壤之上，而是从中汲取养分。我们越是剥夺这些树上的果实，或将它们修剪成我们偏爱的模样，它们就越发显得雄伟壮丽、硕果累累。

Myths, told for their own sake, are not stories that have meanings, but stories that give meanings.

神话本身并非有意义的故事，而是赋予意义的故事。

96

Storytellers become metaphysicians, or ideologists, when they come to believe they know the entire story of a people. This is history theatricalized, with the beginning and end in plain sight. A psychoanalyst who looks for the Freudian myth in patients imposes a filter that lets through nothing the psychoanalyst was not prepared to find.

当讲故事的人自认为掌握了一个民族的全部历史时，他们就变成了形而上学家或意识形态家。这是一种戏剧化的历史，开头和结尾都清晰可见。精神分析师如果试图在病人身上寻找弗洛伊德式的神话，就会设置一个过滤器，让所有他自己没有预料到的东西都无法通过。

The psychotherapeutic relationship will become horizonal only when both patient and therapist realize that the Freudian myth does not determine the meaning of what happens between them, but offers the possibility that their relationship will have a story of its own.

只有当患者和治疗师都意识到弗洛伊德神话并不能决定他们之间发生的事情的意义，而是提供了他们之间的关系拥有自己故事的可能性时，心理治疗关系才会变成横向的。

The Freudian myth does not therefore repeat itself in their relationship, but resonates in it. Those Jews who claim the right to certain territories on the basis of a biblical promise, those Christians who believe the Russians are the great evil armies foreseen in biblical prophecies of the end of the world, repeat the bible but do not resonate with it.

因此，弗洛伊德的神话并没有在他们的关系中重现，而是在其中产生了共鸣。那些声称对某些领土拥有权利的犹太人，那些认为俄罗斯人是圣经预言中世界末日邪恶大军的基督徒，他们虽然在重复圣经，但并没有真正理解圣经的含义。

We resonate with myth when it resounds in us. A myth resounds in me when its voice is heard in mine but not heard as mine. I do not resonate when I quote Jeremiah or when I speak as Jeremiah, but only when Jeremiah speaks in a way that touches an original voice in me. The speech of New Yorkers resonates not because they talk like New Yorkers, but because when they talk we hear New York in their voice.

我们与神话产生共鸣，是因为它在我们心中回响。对我而言，神话的共鸣在于它的声音在我心中回荡，却并非以我自己的声音呈现。我引用耶利米的话语，或以耶利米的口吻说话，并不会让我产生共鸣；只有当耶利米的话语触动了我内心深处那原始的声音时，我才会产生共鸣。纽约人的语言之所以能引起共鸣，并非因为他们说话的方式像纽约人，而是因为当他们说话时，我们能从他们的声音中听到纽约的气息。

The resonance of myth collapses the apparent distinction between the story told by one person to another and the story of their telling and listening. It is one thing for you to tell me the story of Muhammad; it is quite another for me to tell the story of your telling me about Muhammad. Ordinarily we confine the story to the words of the speaker. But in doing so we treat it as a story quoted, not a story told. In your relating, and not repeating, the story of Muhammad, I am touched, and I respond from my genius. Something has begun. But in touching, you are also touched. Something has begun between us. Our relationship has opened forward dramatically. Since this drama emerged from the telling of the story of Muhammad, our story resonates with Muhammad’s, and Muhammad’s with ours.

神话的共鸣消弭了人与人之间讲述故事和聆听故事之间看似存在的界限。你向我讲述穆罕默德的故事是一回事，我讲述你向我讲述穆罕默德的故事又是另一回事。通常，我们把故事局限于讲述者的言语。但这样做，我们就把它当作一个被引用的故事，而不是一个被讲述的故事。你讲述穆罕默德的故事，而不是重复它，这深深地打动了我，我的灵感也随之涌现。某种东西开始了。而在这触动中，你也同样被触动。某种东西在我们之间开始了。我们的关系戏剧性地向前发展。既然这戏剧性源于穆罕默德故事的讲述，那么我们的故事就与穆罕默德的故事产生共鸣，穆罕默德的故事也与我们的故事产生共鸣。

As myths are told, and continue to resound in the telling, they come to us already richly resonant. The stories they are sound deeply with the stories of their telling. Their strength as stories lies in their ability to invite us into their drama. It is a drama that contains an entire history of voices, sounding and resounding from a thousand sources in our culture. For this reason myths are significantly unresolved—but unresolved in the way of an infinite game, having rules, or narrative structure, that allow any number of participants at any time to enter the drama without fixing its plot or bringing it to closure in a final scene. In such stories much will be said about closure, or death, but their telling will always disclose the way death comes in the course of play and not at its end.

神话在口口相传中不断回响，它们本身就蕴含着丰富的内涵。故事本身与讲述它们的故事紧密相连，彼此交融，浑然一体。它们的力量在于能够邀请我们进入其中，感受那跌宕起伏的戏剧。这戏剧包含了我们文化中无数声音的历史，它们在千百个源头回荡，经久不息。正因如此，神话往往充满未解之谜——但这种未解之谜如同一个无限循环的游戏，它拥有规则或叙事结构，允许任意数量的参与者随时加入其中，而无需设定固定的情节或以最终的场景来结束它。在这样的故事中，人们会谈论结局或死亡，但它们的讲述总是会揭示，死亡是在游戏过程中悄然降临，而非在故事的终点。

97

Myths of irrepressible resonance have lost all trace of an author. Even when sacred texts are written down by an identifiable prophet or evangelist, it is invariably thought that these words were first spoken to their recorders and not spoken by them. Moses received the law and did not compose it. Muhammad heard the Quran and did not dictate it. Christians do not read Mark but the gospel according to Mark. Hindus understand their most authoritative texts, the Vedas, to be heard (sruti), and the literature that derives from the Vedas to be composed (smriti).

那些具有强大感染力的神话早已失去了作者的踪迹。即使是那些由可辨识的先知或传道者记录下来的神圣文本，人们也总是认为这些文字最初是口述给记录者的，而不是由他们自己说的。摩西接受了律法，而不是自己撰写的。穆罕默德聆听了《古兰经》，而不是自己口述的。基督徒阅读的不是《马可福音》，而是根据《马可福音》所作的福音书。印度教徒认为他们最权威的经典——吠陀经——是需要聆听（sruti）的，而源自吠陀经的文献则是需要创作（smriti）的。

The gospel can be heard nowhere except from those who themselves have heard it. Although I might hear New York in your voice, there is no possibility I could hear New York by itself. No myth, therefore, exists by itself; neither does it have a discoverable origin. Whom could we name as the first New Yorker? Even when it is God who is heard by the prophet, it is a god who speaks in the language and idiom of the prophet, and not in locutions restricted to divine utterance—as though that god’s speaking were itself a form of listening.

福音只能从那些亲耳聆听过它的人那里听到。虽然我可能从你的声音中听到纽约，但我不可能单独听到纽约。因此，任何神话都不是孤立存在的，它的起源也无法追溯。我们能说出谁是第一个纽约人吗？即使先知听到的是上帝的旨意，那也是上帝用先知的语言和习语说话，而不是用仅限于神圣话语的措辞——仿佛上帝的言语本身就是一种聆听。

Indeed, myth is the highest form of our listening to each other, of offering a silence that makes the speech of the other possible. This is why listening is far more valued by religion than speaking. Fides ex auditu. Faith comes by listening, Paul said.

的确，神话是我们彼此聆听的最高形式，它以一种沉默的方式，使对方的言语成为可能。这就是为什么宗教更重视聆听而非言语。“信仰源于聆听，”保罗说。

98

The opposite of resonance is amplification. A choir is the unified expression of voices resonating with each other; a loudspeaker is the amplification of a single voice, excluding all others. A bell resonates, a cannon amplifies. We listen to the bell, we are silenced by the cannon.

共鸣的反义词是放大。合唱团是众人声音相互共鸣的统一表达；扬声器则是放大单一声音，排除其他声音。钟声产生共鸣，大炮则放大声音。我们聆听钟声，大炮声则使我们噤声。

When a single voice is sufficiently amplified, it becomes a speaking that makes it impossible for any other voices to be heard. We do not listen to a loudspeaker for what is being said, but only because it is all that is being said. Magisterial speech is amplified speech; it is speech that silences. Loud-speaking is a mode of command, and therefore a speech designed to bring itself to an end as completely and swiftly as possible. The amplified voice seeks obedient action on the part of its hearers and an immediate end to their speech. There is no possibility of conversation with a loudspeaker.

当一个人的声音被放大到一定程度时，它就变成了一种喧嚣的宣讲，其他任何声音都无法被听到。我们听扩音器说话，并非为了听它说了什么，而是因为那是唯一被宣讲的声音。权威的演讲就是被放大的演讲；它是一种令人噤声的演讲。大声演讲是一种命令的方式，因此，它的目的是尽快、彻底地结束。被放大的声音寻求听众的服从，并希望演讲立即结束。与扩音器对话是不可能的。

Ideology is the amplification of myth. It is the assumption that since the beginning and end of history are known there is nothing more to say. History is therefore to be obediently lived out according to the ideology. Just as the warmakers of Europe regularly melted down the bells to recast them into cannon, the metaphysicians have found the meaning of their myths and announced those meanings without their narrative resonance. The myths themselves are now regarded as falsehoods or curiosities, and are therefore to be disregarded, if not forbidden.

意识形态是对神话的放大。它假定，既然历史的始末已知，那就没有什么可说的了。因此，历史应当按照意识形态的指引而顺从地演绎。正如欧洲的战争制造者经常熔化钟铃重铸成大炮一样，形而上学家们也找到了神话的意义，并宣布这些意义，却忽略了它们原有的叙事共鸣。如今，神话本身被视为谎言或奇闻异事，因此应该被忽视，甚至应该被禁止。

What ideologists are concerned to hide is the choral nature of history, the sense that it is a symphony of very different, even opposed, voices, each nonetheless making the other possible.

意识形态家们竭力掩盖的是历史的合唱性质，是各种截然不同甚至相互对立的声音交响曲，而每一种声音都使另一种声音成为可能。

99

If it is true that myth provokes explanation, then it is also true that explanation’s ultimate design is to eliminate myth. It is not just that the availability of bells in churches and town halls of Europe makes it possible to forge new cannon; it is that the cannon are forged in order to silence the bells. This is the contradiction of finite play in its highest form: to play in such a way that all need for play is erased.

如果说神话确实会引发解释，那么解释的最终目的也恰恰在于消除神话。欧洲教堂和市政厅里钟声的出现，并非仅仅为锻造新炮提供了可能；而是锻造新炮的目的正是为了使钟声沉寂。这正是有限游戏最高形式的矛盾：以一种最终消除一切游戏需求的方式进行游戏。

The loudspeaker, successfully muting all other voices and therefore all possibility of conversation, is not listened to at all, and for that reason loses its own voice and becomes mere noise. Whenever we succeed in being the only speaker, there is no speaker at all. Julius Caesar originally sought power in Rome because he loved to play the very dangerous style of politics common to the Republic; but he played the game so well that he destroyed all his opponents, making it impossible for him to find genuinely dangerous combat. He was unable to do the very thing for which he sought power. His word was now irresistible, and for that reason he could speak with no one, and his isolation was complete. “We might almost say this man was looking for an assassination” (Syme).

扩音器成功地屏蔽了所有其他声音，从而消除了所有对话的可能性，却无人倾听，因此失去了自身的存在，沦为噪音。当我们成功地成为唯一的发言者时，实际上就不存在发言者了。尤利乌斯·凯撒最初在罗马寻求权力，是因为他喜欢玩弄共和国时期常见的危险政治手段；但他玩得太过火，以至于消灭了所有对手，使他无法再遇到真正危险的挑战。他无法做他追求权力的初衷。他的话语如今无人能挡，因此他无法与任何人交谈，彻底与世隔绝。“我们几乎可以说，这个人就是在寻求暗杀”（赛姆）。

If we are to say that all explanation is meant to silence myth itself, then it will follow that whenever we find people deeply committed to explanation and ideology, whenever play takes on the seriousness of warfare, we will find persons troubled by myths they cannot forget they have forgotten. The myths that cannot be forgotten are those so resonant with the paradox of silence they become the source of our thinking, even our culture, and our civilization.

如果我们认为所有解释的目的都是为了消除神话本身，那么由此便可得出结论：每当我们发现有人深陷于解释和意识形态之中，每当游戏变得如同战争般严肃时，我们都会发现有人被那些他们无法忘记的、早已被遗忘的神话所困扰。这些无法被遗忘的神话，正是那些与沉默悖论产生如此强烈共鸣的神话，它们成为了我们思想、文化乃至文明的源泉。

These are the myths we can easily discover and name, but whose meanings continually elude us, myths whose conversion to truth never quite fills the bells of their resonance with the sand of metaphysical interpretation. These are often exceedingly simple stories. Abraham is an example. Although only two children were born to Abraham in his long life, and one of those was illegitimate, he was promised that his descendents would be as numberless as the stars of the heavens. All three of the West’s major religions consider themselves children of Abraham, though each has often understood to be itself the only and final family of the patriarch, an understanding always threatened by the resounding phrase: numbered as the stars of the heavens. This is the myth of a future that always has a future; there is no closure in it. It is a myth of horizon.

这些神话我们很容易发现并命名，但它们的意义却始终难以捉摸；这些神话的真理化，永远无法完全填满它们共鸣的钟声，也无法被形而上学的诠释所完全诠释。这些故事往往极其简单。亚伯拉罕的故事就是一个例子。尽管亚伯拉罕一生只有两个孩子，其中一个还是私生子，但他却被许诺他的后裔将如同天上的繁星般无数。西方三大宗教都自认为是亚伯拉罕的后裔，尽管它们各自也常常认为自己是这位先祖唯一且最终的传承家族，但这种理解始终受到那句响亮的短语的挑战：“如同天上的繁星般无数”。这是一个关于未来的神话，它永远没有终点，没有尽头。这是一个关于地平线的神话。

The myth of the Buddha’s enlightenment has the same paradox in it, the same provocation to explanation but with as little possibility of settling the matter. It is the story of a mere mortal, completely without divine aid, undertaking successfully a spiritual quest for release from all forms of bondage, including the need to report this release to others. The perfect unspeakability of this event has given rise to an immense flow of literature in scores of languages that shows no signs of abating.

佛陀证悟的神话也蕴含着同样的悖论，同样引人深思，亟待解释，却又几乎不可能得到解答。这是一个凡人，完全没有神助，成功地完成了一场精神之旅，最终摆脱了一切束缚，包括必须将这种解脱告知他人。这一事件的不可思议之处，催生了无数以多种语言写成的浩瀚文学作品，而且丝毫没有减弱的迹象。

Perhaps the Christian myth has been the narrative most disturbing to the ideological mind. It is, like those of Abraham and the Buddha, a very simple tale: that of a god who listens by becoming one of us. It is a god “emptied” of divinity, who gave up all privilege of commanding speech and “dwelt among us,” coming “not to be served, but to serve,” “being all things to all persons.” But the worlds to which he came received him not. They no doubt preferred a god of magisterial utterance, a commanding idol, a theatrical likeness of their own finite designs. They did not expect an infinite listener who joyously took their unlikeness on himself, giving them their own voice through the silence of wonder, a healing and holy metaphor that leaves everything still to be said.

或许，基督教神话是最令意识形态人士感到不安的叙事。它如同亚伯拉罕和佛陀的故事一样，讲述的是一个非常简单的故事：一位神为了倾听而化身为我们中的一员。这位神“舍弃”了神性，放弃了所有发号施令的特权，“住在我们中间”，来到我们中间“不是为了被人服侍，而是为了服侍人”，“成为所有人的一切”。然而，他所到之处，世人却并不接纳他。他们无疑更倾向于一位拥有威严话语权的神，一个威严的偶像，一个戏剧化的、反映他们自身有限图景的形象。他们没有预料到，会有一位无限的倾听者，欣然接受他们的不同之处，通过充满惊奇的静默，赋予他们自己的声音——这是一种疗愈而神圣的隐喻，其中一切仍有待表达。

Those Christians who deafened themselves to the resonance of their own myth have driven their killing machines through the garden of history, but they did not kill the myth. The emptied divinity whom they have made into an Instrument of Vengeance continues to return as the Man of Sorrows bringing with him his unfinished story, and restoring the voices of the silenced.

那些对自身神话的回响充耳不闻的基督徒，驾驶着杀戮机器穿梭于历史的花园，但他们并未扼杀神话本身。他们所塑造的、被掏空的、沦为复仇工具的神性，依然以悲伤之子的形象回归，带来他未竟的故事，并唤醒那些被噤声者的声音。

100

The myth of Jesus is exemplary, but not necessary. No myth is necessary. There is no story that must be told. Stories do not have a truth that someone needs to reveal, or someone needs to hear. It is part of the myth of Jesus that it makes itself unnecessary; it is a narrative of the word becoming flesh, of language entering history; a narrative of the word becoming flesh and dying, of history entering language. Who listens to his myth cannot rise above history to utter timeless truths about it.

耶稣的神话堪称典范，但并非必要。任何神话都并非必要。没有哪个故事是必须讲述的。故事本身并不包含需要揭示或聆听的真理。耶稣的神话恰恰在于它本身的不必要性；它讲述的是道成肉身，语言融入历史；讲述的是道成肉身并最终死去，历史融入语言。聆听他神话的人无法超越历史，也无法从中领悟永恒的真理。

It is not necessary for infinite players to be Christians; indeed it is not possible for them to be Christians—seriously. Neither is it possible for them to be Buddhists, or Muslims, or atheists, or New Yorkers—seriously. All such titles can only be playful abstractions, mere performances for the sake of laughter.

无限多的玩家不必都是基督徒；事实上，他们根本不可能成为基督徒——说真的。他们也不可能成为佛教徒、穆斯林、无神论者或纽约人——说真的。所有这些头衔都只能是戏谑的抽象概念，纯粹是为了博君一笑而进行的表演。

Infinite players are not serious actors in any story, but the joyful poets of a story that continues to originate what they cannot finish.

无限的玩家在任何故事中都不是严肃的演员，而是快乐的故事诗人，他们不断地创造着他们无法完成的故事。

101

There is but one infinite game.

世上只有一场无限的游戏。
